article_html:
The recent change of government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa raises a question for anyone interested in Pakistan’s politics and society. Why did the removal of a popular PTI government produce so little visible resistance?

Many analysts expected a strong reaction in the party’s provincial stronghold. PTI-backed candidates had won an overwhelming share of seats in KP, and subsequent Gallup surveys continued to indicate the party’s popularity. Some expected voters to take to the streets. Others anticipated bureaucratic hurdles: resignations, ministers refusing to hand over power, confrontation between provincial police and federal forces and a transition requiring a heavy-handed crackdown.

There have been minor reports of protests in Khyber and arrests, including, worryingly, of the chief minister and other political figures. Yet the larger transition appeared considerably smoother than many had predicted. There was no widespread uprising of the kind that some PTI voices had warned would follow the crossing of a red line.

This article is not an assessment of the legality or morality of the emergency. The question here is analytical: why did the change happen with comparatively little visible resistance, and what does that tell us about politics and public attitudes?

Immediately after the proclamation, Gallup Pakistan conducted a snap poll nationally and in KP. The findings suggested a divided public, with substantial support for and opposition to the emergency and a significant number of respondents unwilling to take a position. On the question of how to respond, around 80% nationally, in KP and within PTI circles favoured a legal route over protest. In other words, data also suggested limited appetite for protest.

I would offer four possible explanations for the gap between the expectation of resistance and what actually happened. First, resentment, disappointment and discontent do not automatically become political action. Individuals can be dissatisfied, neighbourhoods can be dissatisfied, and biradaris can be dissatisfied. To translate that sentiment into collective action capable of producing an outcome, much more is required. This is one reason political parties and other political organisations exist.

Without Imran Khan, the PTI has struggled to act as a cohesive political organisation. Some would argue that, despite its appeal as an iconoclastic force offering a break from dynastic politics and individual whims, the PTI has become even more dependent on one individual than some of the parties it challenged. Much of its vote is identified with Khan personally. Other party leaders, including provincial chief ministers, seem to command little loyalty or political appeal, so the incentive for them to rise is close to non-existent.

That matters for mobilisation. A call to defend Imran Khan himself may carry a very different appeal from a call to defend an individual provincial leader. If the party’s political figures cannot persuade voters that their displacement is equivalent to an attack on Khan, it is much harder to turn his popularity into sustained action on the streets. The event has shown that popularity does not automatically translate into people coming out to protect the government or becoming its defenders unless party mechanics are in place and well oiled.

The second explanation is fragmentation. The PTI leadership has been divided among competing centres of influence: the former and more recently deposed chief ministers and their supporters; figures around Imran Khan’s sisters and his wife; and provincial and national leadership groups. Tensions have also emerged among office holders within the party. The complete silence, even to the extent of press conferences, from the Punjab leg of the PTI is also being questioned. These divisions make collective action harder to coordinate.

Some may see the absence of a stronger party structure as a failure of leadership from Imran Khan. Others may argue that keeping potential successors divided has helped preserve Khan’s central position. The latter is a possible interpretation, not an established account of his motives. Whatever the explanation, the result is that a party with an enormous popular following has struggled to present a unified organisational response.

The 2024 election showed the strength of voters’ commitment, even when the establishment went against the PTI. But an election and a sustained protest make different demands. Voters can make an individual decision in a polling booth; a successful protest movement requires leadership, coordination, resources, and a shared strategy that goes far beyond casting a single vote.

A third possibility concerns the constitution’s place in the public imagination. Even where democratic values are not fully embedded, the idea of constitutional procedure and rule of law may retain legitimacy. The emergency was presented through a formal constitutional process involving presidential proclamation and parliamentary approval. That appearance may have encouraged officials to comply and some citizens to favour legal remedies.

The fourth point is that the PTI’s seat dominance is easily mistaken for unanimous support. The party and its supporters often cite their overwhelming share of seats as evidence that virtually the whole province stands behind them. 

Yet, on the estimate cited here, PTI-backed candidates received around 45% of the vote in KP in the 2024 election, while the remainder went to other candidates and parties. The JUI, on the same account, was a distant second at around 18%. These figures require confirmation against the relevant election results and vote denominator.

Voters who chose other parties do not necessarily actively oppose the PTI or support its removal. It does mean that a near-monopoly of assembly seats should not be confused with unanimous public opinion.

All four explanations operate in an environment in which protest can be costly. Arrests, repression and uncertainty about personal safety shape the calculations of voters and political workers. Repression alone, however, may not explain the full absence of political expression. The four reasons shared earlier have played a crucial role.

Nor is the absence of a mass uprising unique to the PTI. The removal of elected governments in Pakistan has often failed to produce a mobilisation proportional to their electoral support. Nawaz Sharif’s removal in the 1999 military coup is one example. Earlier dismissals of elected governments, including those of Benazir Bhutto and Nawaz Sharif, also provide grounds to examine the limits of public resistance. The PTI’s claims of exceptional popularity did not necessarily exempt it from the conditions that constrained other parties when they lost power. PTI leadership, including Imran Khan, has perhaps misjudged this limitation.

For the PTI, the experience suggests that confrontation without dialogue — with the establishment and with other political actors — has limited prospects. For the establishment, the orderly transition may show an immediate advantage. It should not be interpreted as a blank cheque or proof that the underlying dispute has disappeared.

In the longer run, the grievances of the people represented by the PTI cannot be resolved simply through administrative control. They require political engagement and reform, including reflection within state institutions.

The writer is executive director of Gallup Pakistan and holds a Masters degree from the School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS), London.

headline: Gisele Bündchen celebrates major honour with husband by her side
subheadline: Gisele Bündchen and Joaquim Valente share rare Halloween looks
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Gisele Bündchen and Joaquim Valente traded their usual polished looks for cowboy style, but their night out had a much bigger purpose than Halloween fun.

The couple attended Lotus House’s annual gala in Miami on Thursday, October 29, where the supermodel and Karlie Kloss were honoured with the “It Takes a Village” award for their support of the women and children’s shelter.

Read More: Gisele Bündchen returns to VS show in surprise appearance

Bündchen arrived in a plaid shirt, jeans and a cowboy hat, styling her hair in two braids. Valente joined the Western theme in a tan shirt, brown vest and buckle belt.

The two looked ready for a country-themed night out — with a charitable cause at the center of it all.

“I’m so grateful to be part of the Lotus House family, where an incredible team and volunteers work with so much love to give women and children hope for a brighter future,” she said in a press statement.

“It reminds me that even the smallest acts of kindness can grow into something extraordinary.”

The model later shared photos from the evening on Instagram, adding another message about the importance of giving back.

“If there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that kindness works like a seed,” she said.

“Even the smallest act can make a difference. When we show up for one another, we don’t just plant hope, we help it grow into something extraordinary.”

The outing also offered a glimpse of the couple’s life together. Bündchen and Valente married in an intimate ceremony in December 2025, after welcoming their first child together in February that year.

Read More: Gisele Bündchen's true feelings on Tom Brady's new love laid bare

A source previously told Peopel magazine that Bündchen feels “really happy being married,” adding that the milestone made their everyday life feel more meaningful.

headline: Harry Styles dresses as Elvis Presley for 'Harryween' night
subheadline: Harry Styles channels Elvis in white jumpsuit as Zoë Kravitz and Riley Keough watch on
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Harry Styles has dressed as Elvis Presley for the first night of his Harryween concerts at Madison Square Garden in New York.

The singer opened the two-night Halloween celebration on Friday 30 October in a “bedazzled” white jumpsuit with colourful embellishments and a cape.

The look was a nod to the rock ’n’ roll icon’s famously flamboyant stage outfits.

Read more: Spotify plans free dance party 'Harryween' for Harry Styles fans

Among the audience was Styles’ fiancée, the actress Zoë Kravitz, 37, who watched from the crowd in a red devil costume with matching horns.

She was joined by her longtime friend Riley Keough, 37, who is Elvis Presley’s granddaughter, the daughter of Lisa Marie Presley and Danny Keough.

Videos from the night show both watching from the audience, with Keough filming the performance on her phone.

Styles and Kravitz were first linked in the summer of 2025, and the couple are reported to have become engaged in April after Kravitz was seen wearing a diamond ring.

The concert was part of Styles’ Together, Together residency, a 30-show run in New York City. The two Harryween nights, on 30 and 31 October, bring it to a close.

Harryween has become a tradition for fans.

Styles hosted the first in 2021 during his Love on Tour, also over two nights at Madison Square Garden.

In 2022, he performed in Los Angeles as Danny Zuko from Grease in an all-black Gucci outfit. This year’s run finishes on Halloween night, with the singer’s costume for the final show yet to be revealed.

Read more: Harry Styles announces release date for 'Coming Up Roses' music video

headline: Imperiled pregnancies: How heat storms threaten mothers and babies
subheadline: Medical research has found that heat can correlate with weaker babies, sicker mothers, and more babies born prematurely
author: Reuters
article_text:
Over the last six-and-a-half decades, heat waves have morphed from intermittent irritations into globe-spanning events that can last months or even years – what Reuters calls “heat storms.” While these supersized heat waves affect virtually everyone, among the most vulnerable are pregnant women and fetuses.

Medical research has found that heat can correlate with weaker babies, sicker mothers, and more babies born prematurely. Reuters conducted its own analysis of more than eight million births in Mexico, finding that when hot-season heat storms or heatwaves hit during the last month of pregnancy, the rate of preterm births rises by as much as 18%.

Here are the key findings of Reuters’ investigation into how heat storms hurt the world’s pregnancies:

1. Heat storms have become a major global threat

Until now, there has been no universally accepted definition of a heat wave. So, in consultation with climate scientists, Reuters developed our own.

By our definition, a heat wave is five consecutive days of heat in the top 10% of the historical range for an area. We call the largest heat waves – those that cover at least 1% of the globe at their peak, about half the size of Canada – heat storms.

By analyzing temperature data for every hour of every day since 1960, Reuters revealed that they are mushrooming in size and number. The 1960s saw just 50 heat storms – this decade, there have already been more than 665. The biggest drifted over nearly 85% of the planet in its year-long lifespan, affecting virtually every person in the world.

How heat waves have grown

The largest heat wave of the 1960s reached about 6% of the planet and lasted 46 days. By contrast, the largest heat wave this decade swept over 85% of the globe during its 367-day lifetime. Reuters calls such massive heat waves, those that cover at least 1% of the planet, “heat storms,” and they have expanded dramatically in number and size.

2. Heat storms are especially risky for pregnant women

Recent research has tied heat waves to severe pregnancy complications. Spikes in heat are associated with higher odds of dangerous hypertension, birth defects, miscarriage and stillbirth.

While there seem to be absolute temperatures at which heat becomes dangerous, researchers are particularly concerned about unusual heat: Every 1 degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit) above what a woman is used to has been found to correlate with harm.

The clearest connection is with preterm birth, which can have severe lifelong health effects. Reuters analyzed millions of birth records from Mexico – which publishes detailed birth data – and found that as exposure to hot-season heat storms and heat waves increases in the last month of pregnancy, so too does the rate of preterm birth.

Preterm births rise sharply with heat storms and heat waves

Reuters analyzed more than 8 million births in Mexico from 2008 to 2025. We found that the rate of preterm births increased with more exposure to hot-season heat storms and heat waves during the last month of pregnancy. Among women with no exposure to heat storms or heat waves during the hot season, 7.2% of births were preterm.

3. The threat from heat storms is global

Heat waves cause problems for pregnant women throughout the world and across vastly different climates.

In Mexico, for example, Reuters found that heat waves and heat storms are linked to increases in preterm birth among expectant mothers across states with searing deserts, humid jungles, and temperate mountain plateaus.

Scientific studies have identified heat-related complications among pregnant women from China and Australia to South Africa and the United States.

4. It’s unclear why heat causes harm – and what works best to protect against it

Because the science is still new, scientists are trying to determine how heat hurts pregnancies. Some suggest high temperatures prompt the body to redirect blood from the placenta to cool a mother or that heat increases the strain on a fetus’s heart, among other potential pathways.

Researchers are now trying to answer those questions – and identify the best interventions to help expectant mothers. While we wait for clear answers, health workers from Johannesburg to Miami are stepping in with protections that range from wide-brimmed hats and white-painted roofs to air conditioning units.

5. “Everyone is at risk,” an expert told Reuters. That included her, too

One of the doctors studying the risk that heat waves pose to pregnant women is Darshnika Lakhoo, who co-wrote a 2024 review article synthesizing the science for Nature Medicine, one of the world’s leading medical journals.

While writing that paper, Lakhoo sweltered through her own heat wave-blistered pregnancy. She was carrying twins, which is its own risk factor for various complications, including preterm birth. But research shows that heat waves can amplify pre-existing conditions. Lakhoo suffered three severe pregnancy complications and eventually gave birth six weeks early.

“No one is going to be safe in a warming world,” said Lakhoo. “And especially not pregnant women.”

Over the last six-and-a-half decades, heat waves have morphed from intermittent irritations into globe-spanning events that can last months or even years – what Reuters calls “heat storms.” While these supersized heat waves affect virtually everyone, among the most vulnerable are pregnant women and fetuses.

Medical research has found that heat can correlate with weaker babies, sicker mothers, and more babies born prematurely. Reuters conducted its own analysis of more than eight million births in Mexico, finding that when hot-season heat storms or heatwaves hit during the last month of pregnancy, the rate of preterm births rises by as much as 18%.

Here are the key findings of Reuters’ investigation into how heat storms hurt the world’s pregnancies:

1. Heat storms have become a major global threat

Until now, there has been no universally accepted definition of a heat wave. So, in consultation with climate scientists, Reuters developed our own.

By our definition, a heat wave is five consecutive days of heat in the top 10% of the historical range for an area. We call the largest heat waves – those that cover at least 1% of the globe at their peak, about half the size of Canada – heat storms.

By analyzing temperature data for every hour of every day since 1960, Reuters revealed that they are mushrooming in size and number. The 1960s saw just 50 heat storms – this decade, there have already been more than 665. The biggest drifted over nearly 85% of the planet in its year-long lifespan, affecting virtually every person in the world.

How heat waves have grown

The largest heat wave of the 1960s reached about 6% of the planet and lasted 46 days. By contrast, the largest heat wave this decade swept over 85% of the globe during its 367-day lifetime. Reuters calls such massive heat waves, those that cover at least 1% of the planet, “heat storms,” and they have expanded dramatically in number and size.

2. Heat storms are especially risky for pregnant women

Recent research has tied heat waves to severe pregnancy complications. Spikes in heat are associated with higher odds of dangerous hypertension, birth defects, miscarriage and stillbirth.

While there seem to be absolute temperatures at which heat becomes dangerous, researchers are particularly concerned about unusual heat: Every 1 degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit) above what a woman is used to has been found to correlate with harm.

The clearest connection is with preterm birth, which can have severe lifelong health effects. Reuters analyzed millions of birth records from Mexico – which publishes detailed birth data – and found that as exposure to hot-season heat storms and heat waves increases in the last month of pregnancy, so too does the rate of preterm birth.

Preterm births rise sharply with heat storms and heat waves

Reuters analyzed more than 8 million births in Mexico from 2008 to 2025. We found that the rate of preterm births increased with more exposure to hot-season heat storms and heat waves during the last month of pregnancy. Among women with no exposure to heat storms or heat waves during the hot season, 7.2% of births were preterm.

3. The threat from heat storms is global

Heat waves cause problems for pregnant women throughout the world and across vastly different climates.

In Mexico, for example, Reuters found that heat waves and heat storms are linked to increases in preterm birth among expectant mothers across states with searing deserts, humid jungles, and temperate mountain plateaus.

Scientific studies have identified heat-related complications among pregnant women from China and Australia to South Africa and the United States.

4. It’s unclear why heat causes harm – and what works best to protect against it

Because the science is still new, scientists are trying to determine how heat hurts pregnancies. Some suggest high temperatures prompt the body to redirect blood from the placenta to cool a mother or that heat increases the strain on a fetus’s heart, among other potential pathways.

Researchers are now trying to answer those questions – and identify the best interventions to help expectant mothers. While we wait for clear answers, health workers from Johannesburg to Miami are stepping in with protections that range from wide-brimmed hats and white-painted roofs to air conditioning units.

5. “Everyone is at risk,” an expert told Reuters. That included her, too

One of the doctors studying the risk that heat waves pose to pregnant women is Darshnika Lakhoo, who co-wrote a 2024 review article synthesizing the science for Nature Medicine, one of the world’s leading medical journals.

While writing that paper, Lakhoo sweltered through her own heat wave-blistered pregnancy. She was carrying twins, which is its own risk factor for various complications, including preterm birth. But research shows that heat waves can amplify pre-existing conditions. Lakhoo suffered three severe pregnancy complications and eventually gave birth six weeks early.

“No one is going to be safe in a warming world,” said Lakhoo. “And especially not pregnant women.”

headline: Jessica Lange reveals why Hollywood no longer excites her
subheadline: Jessica Lange opens up about her future after 'American Horror Story'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jessica Lange may have one final Hollywood chapter in mind — and her latest film could be the perfect farewell.

The actress, 77, has hinted that she is considering retirement, describing her latest project, Long Day’s Journey Into Night, as a fitting way to close a career that has spanned five decades.

“I actually feel like I’m coming to an end,” Lange told Rolling Stone in an interview published on October 30. She added that the new adaptation of Eugene O’Neill’s play was “not a bad way to end.”

Read More: Jessica Lange says King Kong was 'not the fantasy'

The two-time Oscar winner isn't ruling out every possibility just yet, though. A few projects remain in development, but she isn't convinced they will happen.

“There are a couple projects that have been in the works forever that may or may not happen. I don’t know. It doesn’t seem easy to get things made anymore. At least not the kind of films that interest me.”

Looking back, Lange described her years working with legendary filmmakers and actors as an extraordinary experience.

“When I think of the directors I worked with: [Bob] Fosse, Bob Rafelson, Costa-Gavras, Tony Richardson, Karel Reisz. I [had] extraordinary opportunities working with great artists,” she said.

But Hollywood hasn't stayed the same, and Lange isn't particularly impressed with every change.

She criticised the distance technology has created between directors and actors on set, saying it has affected the creative atmosphere.

As for how she wants to be remembered, Lange has a simple answer: an “honest actor.”

“I’ve been incredibly lucky. I love acting, and I’ve had decades of being able to do it, which has been a joy for me,” she said.

Read More: Jessica Lange reveals she was initially turned down for King Kong

Lange recently returned for the 13th season of American Horror Story, while Long Day’s Journey Into Night arrived in theaters on September 25.

headline: Prince William, Princess Kate's children end family tradition after update
subheadline: Princess Charlotte, Prince Louis face new dilemma as Prince George to return home 'soon'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William and Princess Catherine’s children would be forced to end a special tradition for the family just ahead of the holidays.

The eldest of the Wales children, Prince George, has begun his boarding school at Eton College and will be coming home during the holiday break.

The Waleses are known for prioritising family time, which is why they have made up many personal traditions that they use as a means to bond.

READ MORE: George, Charlotte, Louis get special permission to break protocol

The Prince of Wales, who recently made an appearance on The Graham Norton Show, had revealed that the family loves Celebrity Traitors.

“I love it, the family love it. Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it,” he said, adding “it’s really good telly”.

However, it seems that they would not have to find a new obsession as the show concluded its season on Friday, thereby ending the autumnal watch for now. The show is expected to return next year, but there is a long wait before that.

The end of one family tradition can also mean a start of a new one. Charlotte and Louis may have been obsessed with this one show, they are likely to find a new one to obsess over.

Moreover, as their brother will be joining them soon for the holidays, it is possible that they will find a fresh new activity to bond over.

READ MORE: Prince William beats Prince Harry to the punch with ‘petty' move

headline: Daytime Emmy Awards 2026: Complete list of winners
subheadline: 'General Hospital' emerges as the night's biggest winner at the 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The 53rd Annual Daytime Emmy Awards took place on Friday, October 30, at the Hollywood Palladium, celebrating excellence in daytime television.

The ceremony honoured the year's outstanding performances and productions across daytime dramas, talk shows, culinary programs, and other categories.

General Hospital emerged as the night's biggest winner, taking home the prestigious award for Outstanding Daytime Drama Series, along with three other awards.

READ MORE: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff file for divorce

Beyond the Gates also enjoyed a successful night, winning four awards, while The Young and the Restless, this year's most-nominated series with 18 nominations, secured three wins.

Among the individual winners, Tamara Tunie won Outstanding Lead Actress in a Daytime Drama Series for Beyond the Gates, while Scott Clifton took home Outstanding Lead Actor for The Bold and the Beautiful. Genie Francis also received the Lifetime Achievement Award.

article_html:
The 53rd Annual Daytime Emmy Awards took place on Friday, October 30, at the Hollywood Palladium, celebrating excellence in daytime television.

The ceremony honoured the year's outstanding performances and productions across daytime dramas, talk shows, culinary programs, and other categories.

General Hospital emerged as the night's biggest winner, taking home the prestigious award for Outstanding Daytime Drama Series, along with three other awards.

headline: Pakistan urges Taliban regime to end repression of women, curb terrorism from Afghan soil
subheadline: Separately, Trump admin detains dozens of Afghan immigrants, plans to deport them to Afghanistan: report
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistani envoy says Taliban regime must fulfil its int'l obligations.
Terrorism at heart of Afghanistan's challenges: Counsellor Ajmal.
Envoy says Islamabad would exercise its right to self-defence.

Pakistan has urged the Afghan Taliban regime to end its repression of women and girls and prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan soil to carry out attacks, saying Kabul must fulfil its international obligations.

Speaking during the Interactive Dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Afghanistan in the Third Committee of the UN General Assembly, Counsellor Muhammad Jawad Ajmal urged the Taliban regime to take decisive action against terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

Pakistan has seen sharp spike in terrorism incidents in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the two provinces bordering Afghanistan, since the Taliban's return to power in 2021.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent militant groups from using Afghan territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan. However, the Afghan Taliban regime has failed to address Pakistan's concerns and remains reluctant to take decisive action against terror outfits.

Meanwhile, Counsellor Ajmal urged the international community to shoulder its responsibilities towards vulnerable Afghan refugees and support efforts for a stable and peaceful Afghanistan.

He observed that the denial of fundamental freedoms and basic dignity to women and girls reflected the Taliban's continued retreat from their international commitments.

Such discriminatory and abusive practices were also inconsistent with Islamic laws, traditions and the fundamental tenets of the Muslim faith, he said.

Highlighting Pakistan's longstanding humanitarian contribution, the envoy noted that Islamabad had hosted millions of Afghan refugees over several decades, often in the absence of adequate international support.

He stressed that the international community must step up and share the responsibility of addressing the refugee situation as Pakistan continues to facilitate vulnerable Afghans within its available capacity.

On the security situation, he underscored that terrorism remained at the heart of Afghanistan's challenges.

He expressed serious concern over the presence and activities of terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

The envoy highlighted the nexus between the Afghan Taliban and terror groups, as well as the role of external actors supporting proxy elements targeting Pakistan and other neighbouring countries.

"The Taliban's continued failure to publicly denounce these groups raised serious questions about their complicity and support," he said.

Referring to Pakistan's actions on March 16, he said that Pakistan had precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure, including drone and ammunition storage facilities used by the outlawed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to target Pakistani civilians.

Pakistani forces had targeted the Afghan Taliban's military installations in Kabul and Nangarhar on the night of March 16.

At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the armed forces "successfully carried out precision airstrikes" as part of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq, targeting military installations in Kabul and Nangarhar.

In his address, Counsellor Ajmal maintained that Pakistan could not remain passive in the face of continued terrorist attacks against its people and national security, saying Islamabad would exercise its right to self-defence, whenever necessary and in accordance with international law, against any threat to its citizens and national security.

US plans to deport Afghan immigrants

Separately, a US official and a coalition of veterans and advocacy groups have said that President Donald Trump's administration plans to deport some Afghan immigrants to Afghanistan.

Many facing removal fled Afghanistan after the 2021 Taliban takeover and US withdrawal, said Shawn VanDiver, head of #AfghanEvac, on Friday.

Some facing deportation are "brothers and sons of men who served alongside US forces, families the Taliban already has every reason to target," VanDiver added.

Over 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported, the New York Times reported, in one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans.

The administration detained dozens of Afghan immigrants in Louisiana and plans to deport them, the newspaper said, adding the first flight is expected as soon as Monday.

Trump says his immigration crackdown and deportation drive aim to improve domestic security.

The Homeland Security Department said it would not confirm future removal operations, citing operational security.

He observed that the denial of fundamental freedoms and basic dignity to women and girls reflected the Taliban's continued retreat from their international commitments.
Such discriminatory and abusive practices were also inconsistent with Islamic laws, traditions and the fundamental tenets of the Muslim faith, he said.

Highlighting Pakistan's longstanding humanitarian contribution, the envoy noted that Islamabad had hosted millions of Afghan refugees over several decades, often in the absence of adequate international support.

He stressed that the international community must step up and share the responsibility of addressing the refugee situation as Pakistan continues to facilitate vulnerable Afghans within its available capacity.
On the security situation, he underscored that terrorism remained at the heart of Afghanistan's challenges.
He expressed serious concern over the presence and activities of terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.
The envoy highlighted the nexus between the Afghan Taliban and terror groups, as well as the role of external actors supporting proxy elements targeting Pakistan and other neighbouring countries.
"The Taliban's continued failure to publicly denounce these groups raised serious questions about their complicity and support," he said.

Referring to Pakistan's actions on March 16, he said that Pakistan had precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure, including drone and ammunition storage facilities used by the outlawed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to target Pakistani civilians.
Pakistani forces had targeted the Afghan Taliban's military installations in Kabul and Nangarhar on the night of March 16.

At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the armed forces "successfully carried out precision airstrikes" as part of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq, targeting military installations in Kabul and Nangarhar.

In his address, Counsellor Ajmal maintained that Pakistan could not remain passive in the face of continued terrorist attacks against its people and national security, saying Islamabad would exercise its right to self-defence, whenever necessary and in accordance with international law, against any threat to its citizens and national security.
US plans to deport Afghan immigrants
Separately, a US official and a coalition of veterans and advocacy groups have said that President Donald Trump's administration plans to deport some Afghan immigrants to Afghanistan.
Many facing removal fled Afghanistan after the 2021 Taliban takeover and US withdrawal, said Shawn VanDiver, head of #AfghanEvac, on Friday.
Some facing deportation are "brothers and sons of men who served alongside US forces, families the Taliban already has every reason to target," VanDiver added.
Over 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported, the New York Times reported, in one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans.
The administration detained dozens of Afghan immigrants in Louisiana and plans to deport them, the newspaper said, adding the first flight is expected as soon as Monday.
Trump says his immigration crackdown and deportation drive aim to improve domestic security.
The Homeland Security Department said it would not confirm future removal operations, citing operational security.

headline: Gen Z protests reach Germany as over 160,000 expected at Halloween rallies
subheadline: Protesters' group says it opposes compulsory ​military service and wants greater investment in education
author: Reuters
article_text:
Protests expected in over 30 German cities.
Youth demands better education, lower living costs.
Some shops board up windows ahead of protests.

More than 160,000 people across Germany are expected to join demonstrations on ​Saturday, organisers say, as a youth-led movement inspired by protests elsewhere in Europe takes to the streets to ‌demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests follow a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country's long-time leader at the ballot box, whilfe protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests, organised by campaign group Gen Z regelt (Gen ​Z takes charge), are planned in 34 cities including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The group says it opposes compulsory ​military service and wants greater investment in education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs.

German ⁠authorities say they expect Saturday's demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, to be largely peaceful but have warned of attempts by ​extremist groups to exploit the movement.

Parts of Germany's far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined ​efforts to mobilise support, according to the federal interior ministry.

"We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers," said Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Germany's financial hub, Frankfurt.

"France must not ​be held up as a model in this regard."

In Berlin, some businesses along the luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard boarded up windows ​and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations amid concerns about possible unrest.

Gen Z takes charge

For organisers, however, the focus is on what ‌they see ⁠as the growing pressure on younger generations in Europe's largest economy.

"The government has offered no response to our concerns other than to continue making cuts and piling further burdens upon us," said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

"We will continue to exercise our fundamental right to assemble until you stop ignoring us."

The protests come as ​Germany struggles to revive economic growth ​while facing growing pressure ⁠on pensions and public services as baby boomers retire and the working-age population shrinks.

But questions have been raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the ​broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany's national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has ​distanced itself from ⁠the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on November 20.

"We are distancing ourselves from 'Gen Z regelt,' but not from the students themselves, who have legitimate concerns," said BSK secretary-general Amy Kirchhoff on Thursday.

Sean Baker, a student at the Technical University ⁠of Berlin, ​said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention to the ​poor state of buildings on campus.

"When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building," he told Reuters. "Yet this is where we're ​expected to study on a regular basis."

headline: Kanye West, Bianca Censori Halloween outing comes after family revelations
subheadline: Kim Kardasian's co-parenting confession puts Kanye West back in spotlight
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Kanye West and Bianca Censori traded family drama for some Halloween thrills this week, stepping out for a spooky night at Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights in Los Angeles.

West tried to keep a low profile in a black face mask and dark outfit, while Censori went for a leather jacket and furry scarf.

The couple brought along a large group of friends, security staff and VIP guides — because apparently even a haunted house is better without waiting in line.

Read More: Kim Kardashian says parenting with Kanye West 'big burden'

The group reportedly enjoyed The Simpsons Ride, the Fast & Furious simulator and the Terror Tram, featuring the terrifying clown from the Terrifier films.

Their outing comes as Kim Kardashian opens up about the complicated reality of co-parenting with her ex-husband in Jonathan Van Meter’s new biography, Citizen Kim: The Woman Who Created the Future.

Kardashian revealed that she sometimes communicates with West through Censori and has even invited the couple to stay over so their children can spend time with their father.

"It is challenging co-parenting with someone who comes by every few months, but I'm always like, 'Oh, Dad's traveling,' " she said.

She also explained why she continues protecting West’s image in front of their children.

"I still make up stories and protect [the kids] because I want them to think their dad is the greatest. But I invite him over all the time."

Kardashian even offered to host West and Censori over Christmas, despite their difficult history.

"Last Christmas, I said, 'Sleep over on Christmas Eve. Bring your girlfriend.' I'm easy! 'Let's all do Christmas together,' " she said. "And I'll recommend it again this year."

Read More: Are Bianca Censori and Kanye West having kids?

She added that she would put their past conflicts aside so the children could spend time with their father.

headline: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track
subheadline: UN warns progress insufficient to meet goals of 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth's land, oceans
author: AFP
article_text:
YEREVAN: Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements on Friday at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity's destructive toll on nature.

Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.

The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.

Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.

The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth's land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.

"And that's it. Perfect," said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early Saturday.

But the outcome was "not commensurate" with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut early Saturday as the summit drew to a close.

"The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity," Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP, stressing that "nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations."

'Step forward'

The final plenary stretched through Friday night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.

Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.

Veteran COP observer Juliette Landry from the IDDRI think tank told AFP "there was a lot of push and pull in every direction" throughout the summit and "in that context, it's hard to get things accepted".

In a draft agreement of one closely watched text, nations were urged to "accelerate" their efforts and warned that "increased action" was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.

This "represents a positive outcome... and though there are weaknesses, particularly on harmful subsidies, it does represent a step forward," Guido Broekhoven from WWF International told AFP.

Tackling subsidies and other incentives that encourage activities harmful to nature — such as fossil fuels, intensive agriculture and overfishing — was one of the most politically fraught agenda items at the summit.

"Even though the agreed decision text expresses it in weak terms, COP17 saw important political momentum to address harmful financial incentives, including subsidies," An Lambrechts from Greenpeace International told AFP.

A rare fight over science cast a pall over the summit, with a number of countries accused of undermining efforts to approve key reports in scenes that shocked even seasoned negotiators.

"We regret the increasing instances in which scientific evidence and its uptake has been challenged or constrained" by politics, said Swiss negotiator Gabriela Blatter in a statement on behalf of dozens of countries.

"Our delegations fully respect every state's right to safeguard national interest but science is not negotiable".

Finance feud

A separate row revolved around finding new cash sources to fund conservation efforts — another hot-button issue with public budgets under strain amid an energy crisis and conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

The European Union led a charge for wealthy emerging economies such as China to contribute to global conservation efforts, a contentious issue at COP17.

In a sign of possible compromise, another draft text that circulated Friday invited countries outside the developed-country donors to voluntarily join the group.

Outstanding questions over the design of the Cali Fund — a UN mechanism that hoped to attract billions of dollars in corporate contributions but is close to empty — were left unresolved.

"By punting essential decisions to two years from now, parties have all but ensured the fund remains empty until then," said Pakhi Das from the nonprofit organisation Plant-for-the-Planet.

The COP17 summit decided early Saturday that Ecuador would host the next biodiversity talks in 2028 after the South American nation defeated rival candidate Panama in a secret vote.

headline: Bill Belichick, Jordon Hudson split after years of romance: What went wrong?
subheadline: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson remained partners in business despite breakup
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson called it quit after nearly three years of relationship, ending a romance that frequently made headlines because of their 49-year age gap.

The 74-year-old University of North Carolina football coach and the 25-year-old Trouble Cup Enterprises founder, reportedly, ended their relationship in late 2025.

Although the former couple have gone their separate ways romantically, they remain close friends and are committed to continuing their business partnerships.

Neither has publicly disclosed a specific reason for the split. Their relationship, however, faced considerable attention following their April 2025 appearance on CBS Sunday Morning.

During the interview, Hudson shut down questions from journalist Tony Dokoupil about how she and Belichick first met, saying, "We're not talking about this."

For the unversed, Belichick and Hudson reportedly first crossed paths in February 2021 while she was a college student at Bridgewater State University.

They were first spotted together publicly in January 2023, walking through the French Quarter in New Orleans, and were later seen enjoying a dinner date in the city in September that year.

Before his relationship with Hudson, Belichick was involved with Linda Holliday for 16 years. Their separation was confirmed in September 2023.

Hudson, meanwhile, also shared professional ties with the football coach through Trouble Cup Enterprises, which worked with him on reclaiming trademarks associated with his famous Patriots phrases.

headline: King Charles takes decision about historic royal position, not for William
subheadline: Prince William, heir to the throne, not eligible for centuries-old position established by preceding monarch
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles may have exhibited his confidence in Prince William to one day take over the throne, but not every historic role is preserved for the heir to the throne.

Even if it was introduced by one of his great-great grandfathers.

The King honoured a near five centuries old tradition after inducting a member for a prestigious position.

READ MORE: Royal Family's Remembrance Sunday plans revealed

The monarch, who is currently in Guyana as his high-stakes Caribbean tour continues, had approved a new Oxford professor for role that was established by Henry VIII around 485 years ago established in 1541.

Professor Laura Swift has been appointed Regius Professor of Greek at Christ Church College at the University of Oxford, succeeding Professor Gregory Hutchinson.

The historic academic position retains its royal connection centuries after it was by King Henry VIII, making the position 485 years old.

Professor Swift specialises in ancient Greek literature, particularly Greek tragedy and lyric poetry. She is currently Professor of Greek at the University of Oxford and a Fellow and Tutor in Classics at Magdalen College.

She is known for her research into the relationship between Greek tragedy and other forms of choral poetry and for her work on fragmentary ancient texts. Moreover, she also holds many accolades including Hellenic Foundation Thesis Prize, a Philip Leverhulme Prize.

headline: Pakistan knocked out of Hong Kong Sixes 2026 main trophy race
subheadline: Defeat against UAE in opening match sees Pakistan finish second in Group C, ending their hopes of defending the title
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Defending champions Pakistan have been knocked out of the main Cup competition at the ongoing Hong Kong Sixes 2026, ending their bid for a seventh title.

Despite registering a dominant victory over arch-rivals India, a narrow defeat to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in their opening match saw Pakistan finish second in Group C, ending their hopes of defending the title under the tournament's format.

The Abbas Afridi-led side faced an early setback on Friday after losing a thrilling opening fixture against the UAE. Batting first, Pakistan posted a formidable 106 for 3 in their allotted six overs, courtesy of a blistering half-century from their captain, who smashed 53 runs.

However, the UAE produced a remarkable chase, reaching the 107-run target on the final delivery to secure a dramatic one-wicket victory.

Pakistan bounced back emphatically in their second group match against India. The bowling attack restricted the arch-rivals to 88 for 5 before Pakistan chased down the target in just 3.5 overs, finishing at 91 for 2.

Khawaja Nafay led the charge with an aggressive 41, while Afridi chipped in with a quickfire 35 to guide Pakistan to a comprehensive victory.

However, Pakistan were subsequently pushed down to second place in the Group C standings after the UAE defeated India to finish top of the table. India posted 95 runs, which the Emirates side chased down without losing a wicket in just four overs.

Despite their convincing performance against India, the tournament format dictates that only the group winners advance to the main Cup semi-finals, while the runners-up and third-placed teams progress to the Plate and Bowl semi-finals, respectively.

With the UAE winning both their group matches to remain unbeaten, they secured the only semi-final berth from Group C in the main Cup competition.

Pakistan will now compete in the Plate tournament, where they are scheduled to face hosts Hong Kong in the second Plate semi-final on Saturday.

headline: Jennifer Lawrence rules out her probablity of returning to 'X-Men'
subheadline: Jennifer Lawrence reveals why playing Mystique was a nightmare
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jennifer Lawrence might have worn Mystique’s blue skin like a second layer for years, but don’t expect her to squeeze back into that makeup chair anytime soon.

The Oscar winner has made it pretty clear that returning to the X-Men universe is one thing, but going through another exhausting prosthetics transformation is a completely different story.

Asked by Allure if she would ever consider playing Mystique again, Lawrence didn't exactly leave the door wide open.

Read More: Jennifer Lawrence on-set experience sparks important Hollywood conversation

“Never say never, but absolutely fucking not,” she said bluntly.

The actress then explained why the experience was so difficult, recalling the freezing airbrushing, her ticklish skin and the toll the lengthy process took on her sleep and patience.

“You know how air brushing is very cold? And I am ticklish. I learned how little sleep I can operate on and what can happen to the human mind when you’ve actually reached your breaking point. And patience!”

Lawrence played Mystique in four films between 2011 and 2019, but the makeup was never her favourite part.

During a 2014 appearance on The Tonight Show, she even joked about the uncomfortable setup, while admitting that stunts were the highlight.

Her least favourite part? “most certainly the paint.”

She recently revisited the ordeal on Call Her Daddy, revealing the transformation took “eight hours every time” and involved plenty of “body paint and glue.”

Read More: JLaw recalls 'stopping to buy candy' before 'Hunger Games' audition

Even getting ready for the role came at a cost: dyeing her hair multiple colours in one day left it permanently damaged.

headline: Claire Sweeney could replace Jesy Nelson in 'I'm A Celebrity'
subheadline: The actress is said to have a gap in her schedule after leaving Coronation Street in August
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Claire Sweeney has reportedly been approached by I'm A Celebrity....Get Me Out of Here! bosses to join this years show.

The actress, 55, is said to have a gap in her schedule after leaving Coronation Street in August.

Earlier this week, it was reported that ITV was in advanced talks to sign Mariella Frostrup after Jesy Nelson was forced to pull out of the series.

READ MORE: Claire Sweeney issues warning to parents of young children against Roblox

The former Little Mix star, 35, is said to have backed out of her six-figure deal with a 'heavy heart' just weeks before the series launch, to take care of her daughters, amid their battle with Spinal Muscular Atrophy type 1.

Now, TV insiders say Claire is also in the running to head to the jungle.

A source told The Sun: 'Claire is a massive I'm A Celeb fan and has always fancied her chances in the jungle. She was on Corrie when Alan went on the show and spoke to him about how much he enjoyed it.

'Claire has had multiple meetings now with ITV bosses and has cleared her diary to make sure she's free to make the journey to Australia if she makes the final cut.

'ITV are currently deciding their final line-up but Claire has a great chance. She's a soap icon and would be an amazing addition.'

headline: Dillon Brooks ejected after kicking Jamal Murray during Suns' loss to Nuggets
subheadline: The Phoenix are set to play their home opener against the Golden State Warriors on Saturday, October 24, 2026
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks was ejected on Friday night for kicking Jamal Murray in the groin.

The incident happened during the third quarter of a nail-biting game that ended in a 127-120 win for the Nuggets.

Brooks tried a turnaround jumper in the third quarter with Murray guarding, and when Brooks fell backward, he kicked his right leg forward, making contact with Murray.

After officials reviewed the foul, Brooks was twisting the body in pain on the court for a few moments before eventually standing up and staying in the game.

Brooks was first called for an offensive foul, but after officials reviewed the play, he was assessed for a flagrant 2 foul, which leads to an automatic ejection under NBA rules.

At the time of his ejection, he was leading the Suns with 22 points on his 9 out of 12 shooting attempts.

The loss is a tough outcome for the Phoenix, who had to deal with the last moments of the game without one of their primary offensive options.

The Phoenix are set to play their home opener against the Golden State Warriors on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

headline: Pakistan registers 3,900 children with HIV in 18 months
subheadline: WHO and UNAIDS data shows annual new infections rose by 200% from about 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024
author: M. Waqar Bhatti
article_text:
Sindh, Punjab account for 3,680 of 3,900 registered cases.
92,148 of 417,214 people living with HIV registered nationwide.
Pakistan remains among countries with largest hepatitis burden.

ISLAMABAD: A total of 3,900 children tested positive for HIV across the country between January 2025 and June 2026, with Sindh and Punjab reporting 3,680 of these cases, according to a response submitted to the National Assembly, The News reported.

The province-wise figures, provided by the Ministry of National Health Services in response to questions by Dr Sharmila Faruqui and Nuzhat Sadiq, show 1,915 registrations in Sindh and 1,765 in Punjab. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded 139 cases, Balochistan 46, Islamabad 30, Azad Jammu and Kashmir four and Gilgit-Baltistan one.

The health ministry said the latest programme overview estimated 417,214 people were living with HIV, of whom 92,148 had been registered and 67,878 were receiving antiretroviral treatment.

The national ART network has grown to 113 centres, including 15 added in Sindh this year, while HIV testing increased from 37,944 people in 2020 to 374,126 in 2025.

WHO and UNAIDS data cited in the reply show estimated annual new infections rose from about 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024, an increase of around 200%. Pakistan is among the countries with the fastest-growing HIV epidemics in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, the ministry said, while describing the national epidemic as concentrated and general-population prevalence as below 0.1%.

The government said a case-based national HIV dashboard was operating, but Punjab’s separate system was still being integrated. Measures include pre-surgical screening, contact tracing, screening at 14 points of entry and a phased move to reuse-prevention syringes, with restrictions on conventional syringes up to 10cc due to take effect on January 1, 2027.

The replies also set out a decline in the estimated number of children who had received no first dose of pentavalent vaccine. WHO and UNICEF estimates put the number at 396,000 in 2024, down from 651,000 in 2021, while a 2025 third-party survey estimated fewer than 160,000. The ministry said nearly 488,000 children were vaccinated through intensified outreach in 2025 and 147,709 so far in 2026.

Pakistan remains among the countries with the largest hepatitis burden, with about nine million people estimated to be living with hepatitis C and 3.86 million with hepatitis B. The ministry cited more than 48,000 hepatitis-related deaths a year and over 88,000 new hepatitis C infections in 2024, adding a Rs67.77 billion federal-provincial programme aims to screen 82.5 million people and treat confirmed cases by June 2027, with elimination of hepatitis C as a public health threat targeted for 2030.

The ministry estimated 32.4 million people were living with mental health conditions in 2023, up from 30 million in 2019. It counted 1,050 registered psychiatrists nationwide as of January 2026, or about one for every 245,400 people, but said figures for clinical psychologists and other trained mental-health professionals were unavailable.

A 2018 National Nutrition Survey remained the latest official assessment cited in the reply: more than 40% of children were stunted, 18% wasted and 52% of women of reproductive age were anaemic.

Asked about federal nutrition allocations for 2026-27, the ministry listed Rs137 million for patient diets at PIMS facilities but gave no consolidated allocation for maternal and child nutrition or rural primary healthcare.

The government acknowledged that haemophilia data were incomplete. The National Blood Policy estimates 24,000 people may have bleeding disorders of all kinds, while 4,700 patients, including more than 3,000 with haemophilia A, were registered with the Pakistan chapter of the World Federation of Hemophilia. A national patient registry and treatment protocol are targeted for the second quarter of 2027, with no separate federal budget line for haemophilia treatment.

In a separate reply, the ministry said formaldehyde and methanol were not registered as medicines and had no approved use for treating disease or in food and drinks. It said it had no official record confirming their use by vendors, but described ingestion as toxic and potentially fatal, while enforcement against illegal sale or food use rested with provincial authorities.

The ministry also said there was no unified nationwide mechanism to regulate private healthcare fees. In Islamabad, the healthcare regulator had received no complaint about overcharging; a health complaints system through the 1166 helpline was planned for the third week of November.

The replies detailed the August 26 fire at Pims, where 15 newborns were in the nursery and only one was initially rescued. Emergency services were notified about 15 minutes after the fire began and arrived at 7:01am. The ministry acknowledged that the hospital’s fire alarm system was inadequate, adding that eight officials had been suspended and disciplinary proceedings were under way.

Islamabad has two specialised burn facilities, with 20 beds at Pims and 10 at Nescom Hospital, the ministry said.

headline: Prince Harry turns ‘fly on wall' for important discussion after major loss
subheadline: Prince Harry quietly crashes crucial meeting as team tries to navigate major crisis
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles’s younger son, Prince Harry, was seemingly found in a meeting where he was not scheduled to be in, and it was only later when it was realised.

Harry had made a return to public life in the UK and it had been so far a success. However, all that had to come to a halt after distressing news surfaced.

The Duke of Sussex is reportedly taking a break from public life with his wife Meghan Markle after disturbing probe about father-in-law Thomas Markle Sr continues.

READ MORE: Prince Harry makes desperate call to King Charles about Meghan's father

Even though, the Sussexes are taking some time off, Harry is being remembered fondly for some of his antics by one of the beloved figures of England.

Former England captain Chris Robshaw recalled a cheeky incident that had Harry crash an important crisis meeting after a big loss.

While talking about the key events of life and career to i Paper, Chris shared how Harry being a “big, big rugby man” was often around training.

“He just loved to be around the place, mixing it with the players,” he shared. “He was who he was, but he was a very normal guy in that environment.”

The sportsman continued, “I remember we were having a leadership meeting. We had lost our first game in the Six Nations, and that’s crunch time because you can’t win a Grand Slam.

“On Monday morning, it was me coming in with the leadership group of Owen Farrell, Brad Barritt, Dylan Hartley, all the coaches – and Prince Harry just sitting in the corner while we were trying to work out how to get ourselves out of a hole.”

He added that Harry “knew to keep quiet though”.

headline: Inside Chrishell Stause, G Flip's reported relationship struggles
subheadline: Chrishell Stause and G Flip called off their four years of relationship
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Chrishell Stause and G Flip may have announced their breakup with a message of love and respect, but fresh insider claims suggest their relationship had been under pressure for quite some time.

The couple, who spent four years together, reportedly experienced mounting tensions long before confirming their separation.

According to a source who spoke to the Daily Mail, arguments had become a regular part of their relationship, with the insider describing Stause as "clingy" and "demanding."

Read More: Chrishell Stause, G Flip split: Why their relationship ended?

Another source told Page Six that G Flip "got really fed up" and "couldn't take it anymore." The musician reportedly "didn't like the drama."

The claims also point to Stause's career frustrations following her departure from Selling Sunset last year, after nine seasons.

One insider alleged she wanted more of G Flip's attention while the musician was focused on their own career.

"She wanted to be catered to," the source claimed.

Neither star has publicly confirmed these alleged reasons for the split. Their announcement earlier this week painted a more affectionate picture.

"G and I are no longer together, and we have agreed to treat this public separation with love and respect for each other," Stause said in an emotional Instagram video.

She also admitted feeling "like a little bit of a failure," reflecting on her previous marriages, but described her time with G Flip as "amazing."

The reality star said she was still adjusting to "a different ending" and did not have "all the information or the reasons" behind the breakup.

Read More: Chrishell Stause, G Flip call it quits after four years

The pair first met at a Los Angeles Halloween party nearly five years ago, dressed as skeletons. Now, their love story has reached an unexpected final chapter.

headline: Harry Styles recreates his 16-year-old ‘X Factor' audition look at Harryween
subheadline: Harry Styles brings One Direction fans to tears by channelling his ‘X Factor’ audition appearance
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Harry Styles just took concertgoers on a trip down memory lane, leaving One Direction fans emotional.

The Watermelon Sugar hitmaker surprised the live audience at his 2026 Harryween show by transforming into his 16-year-old self.

He recreated his look from the decade old The X Factor audition that changed his life forever.

READ MORE: Harry Styles dresses as Elvis Presley for 'Harryween' night

Performing at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Friday night, October 30, the Golden singer brought back the shy teenager who first captured hearts during his 2010 X Factor audition.

Dressed in an outfit inspired by his younger self, the now 32-year-old performer even delivered the memorable introduction, "I work in a bakery... I'm 16..." as fans were transported back to the beginning of his journey to stardom.

The As It Was vocalist also performed Stevie Wonder's Isn't She Lovely, the song he famously sang during his original audition.

Seeing the global superstar revisit the very moment that introduced him to millions of fans made the performance particularly special, especially for longtime One Direction supporters who have followed his journey since his teenage years.

In another Halloween spectacle, Styles also channelled Elvis Presley earlier in the show, sporting a white pantsuit, cape and gold sunglasses.

Meanwhile, his backing band joined the throwback theme by recreating different iconic fashion eras from the singer's career.

READ MORE: Spotify plans free dance party 'Harryween' for Harry Styles fans

headline: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg says he won't do media training: 'Stay true to myself'
subheadline: 'It’s not like I’m click-baiting or click-farming or whatever the heck people are saying. But it’s like, that’s honestly how I feel' said Lendeborg
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has refused to bow to the criticism, insisting he won’t do media training.

The Warriors rookie is just a week into his NBA career but has had the spotlight on him since his debut game when he confronted Luka Doncic in a trash talk on the Lakers' court last week.

In an interview with the San Francisco Chronicle, Lendeborg explained why he is not interested in getting media training.

“I’m not doing that, man. I’m going to stay true to myself, and be honest. I’ve seen plenty of interviews where people are talking and it’s like, ‘Man, I don’t want to watch this,’ you know what I mean?" said Lendeborg.

"And it’s not like I’m click-baiting or click-farming or whatever the heck people are saying. But it’s like, that’s honestly how I feel,” Lendeborg continued.

“And I’m not gonna lie about it. I’ve never been a liar. So, just tell the truth.”

Since the Warriors’ rookie Lendeborg's call-out of Luka Doncic for frequently complaining to officials has generated much buzz on social media.

Doncic and Lendeborg exchanged heated words throught out the second quarter after a shouting foul was called on Lendeborg while he was guarding the Slovenian star.

In his debut game, Warriors rookie scored 12 points, three rebounds and two assists.

The viral trash talk even led to a famous lip reader weighing in that sent the internet into a frenzy.

Doncic addressed the controversy in a postgame interview, saying, “Everybody knows when somebody starts talking, you got a different me. So that was it.”

The Lakers’ guard Doncic finished with 28 points, eight rebounds, and seven assists, and 3 steals that contributed to the Lakers’ 127-105 win on their season opener.

headline: CDA issues notices over 'unauthorised structures' at JUI-F chief Fazl's residence, seminaries
subheadline: “All the institutions are bent upon victimising an individual,” says Maulana Asjad Mahmood
author: Muhammad Anis
article_text:
CDA warns Fazl’s residence to face demolition and plot allotment cancellation.
Notices issued to three seminaries in Islamabad over illegal construction.
Mahmood alleges govt targeting JUI-F over Peshawar encroachments.

The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has served three separate notices for the removal of alleged illegal structures at Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman's residence in an upscale Islamabad sector and two seminaries reportedly operated by clerics linked to the party, amid a standoff between the government and the opposition party.

The owner of the residence has been directed to remove illegal constructions in the building’s setback area, as well as guard posts and generators installed on state land, within 15 days, The News reported on Saturday.

The federal government has also initiated action against seminaries reportedly run by JUI-F-affiliated clerics. Notices were issued on October 29 to two seminaries in Sector F-8/3 and another in Bilal Town, near Korang Nullah, over alleged construction without approval.

The notice concerning Fazl's residence, dated October 30 and issued by the CDA’s Building Control Section, was pasted outside the property.

It warns that failure to comply could lead to the sealing of the building, demolition of unauthorised structures and cancellation of the allotment of Plot No 7, Street 83, Sector G-6/4, under the CDA Ordinance and Islamabad Capital Territory Building Control Regulations, 2020.

Interestingly, a previous notice seeking the removal of unauthorised constructions inside and outside the residence was issued on March 18, 2019, during the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf government.

Reacting to the notices, Maulana Asjad Mahmood said in a post on X that the CDA had objected to an additional kitchen built in the house’s setback area, a guard cabin and the installation of a generator outside the building.

“All the institutions are bent upon victimising an individual,” he said. Fazlur Rehman residence has frequently served as a venue for political consultations, with several leaders, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and opposition figures, visiting the JUI-F chief to discuss national issues.

The CDA has been carrying out anti-encroachment operations across Islamabad to remove encroachments from public and state land and act against unauthorised construction and other violations.

As per a statement released by the authority earlier this month, the campaign was being carried out in accordance with applicable laws and building regulations, while cases eligible for regularisation or approval would be processed under the prescribed rules.

The federal government has also initiated action against seminaries reportedly run by JUI-F-affiliated clerics. Notices were issued on October 29 to two seminaries in Sector F-8/3 and another in Bilal Town, near Korang Nullah, over alleged construction without approval.

The notice concerning Fazl's residence, dated October 30 and issued by the CDA’s Building Control Section, was pasted outside the property.

It warns that failure to comply could lead to the sealing of the building, demolition of unauthorised structures and cancellation of the allotment of Plot No 7, Street 83, Sector G-6/4, under the CDA Ordinance and Islamabad Capital Territory Building Control Regulations, 2020.

Interestingly, a previous notice seeking the removal of unauthorised constructions inside and outside the residence was issued on March 18, 2019, during the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf government.

Reacting to the notices, Maulana Asjad Mahmood said in a post on X that the CDA had objected to an additional kitchen built in the house’s setback area, a guard cabin and the installation of a generator outside the building.

“All the institutions are bent upon victimising an individual,” he said. Fazlur Rehman residence has frequently served as a venue for political consultations, with several leaders, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and opposition figures, visiting the JUI-F chief to discuss national issues.

The CDA has been carrying out anti-encroachment operations across Islamabad to remove encroachments from public and state land and act against unauthorised construction and other violations. 

As per a statement released by the authority earlier this month, the campaign was being carried out in accordance with applicable laws and building regulations, while cases eligible for regularisation or approval would be processed under the prescribed rules.

headline: Pakistan faces winter gas crisis as Qatar extends LNG force majeure
subheadline: Govt plans to secure 10 LNG cargoes for two peak winter months against estimated requirement of 20
author: Khalid Mustafa
article_text:
QatarEnergy extends force majeure on LNG supplies until December.
Shortfall could trigger supply crunch for power, industrial sectors.
Household gas demand in Punjab and KP projected to rise threefold.

Pakistan is heading towards a severe winter gas crunch as QatarEnergy has further extended its force majeure on LNG supplies until December 29, leaving the government struggling to secure additional cargoes amid soaring demand and tightening supply options, The News reported on Saturday.

The extension threatens to squeeze LNG availability during December and January, when household gas consumption peaks, raising the prospect of severe supply curtailments for the power sector, industries, fertiliser plants, cement factories and CNG stations.

“Yes, Qatar has extended its force majeure on LNG supplies until the end of December,” Federal Minister for Petroleum and Natural Resources Ali Pervaiz Malik confirmed to The News.

The government is now planning to arrange 10 LNG cargoes for the two peak winter months against an estimated requirement of 20, comprisingnine in December and 11 in January.

The shortfall is likely to intensify competition between domestic consumers, industry and the power sector, with household supplies expected to receive priority, potentially leaving industrial consumers with restricted gas availability.

Senior officials of the Sui gas companies said household gas demand in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could jump from 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) to 1,500 mmcfd during December and January. In Sindh and Balochistan, domestic demand is projected to double from 300 mmcfd to 600 mmcfd.

headline: Queen Camilla's unexpected gesture with powerful message: Details inside
subheadline: Camilla left royal fans emotional with her telling move after King's confession
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Queen Camilla left royal fans emotional as she reminded them of Princess Diana, not in competition, but in a moment that spoke volumes about love, courage and resilience.

Just one year after Princess Diana stunned the world in her iconic Christina Stambolian ‘revenge dress’ in 1994, Camilla Parker Bowles stepped out at The Ritz in a remarkably similar off-the-shoulder look.

It was 1995, a year after then-Prince Charles had confessed he had been unfaithful in his marriage to Diana.

For his first high-society outing with his then-girlfriend Camilla, the pair chose a party for Lady Sarah Keswick at The Ritz, the woman who would later become one of Camilla’s official Queen’s Companions in 2022.

It was the first time the newly-divorced 48-year-old Camilla was seen at the same event as Charles. They arrived 90 minutes apart and left separately, carefully orchestrating every move.

However, the move was never about overshadowing Diana whose grace and legacy remains unmatched and forever loved. No one could ever dim Diana's grace. She will forever remain the People's Princess, loved and respected across the world, and especially cherished by Princes William and Harry and millions of royal fans.

It might simply be an announcement of her daring and unshaking love, romance and steadfast loyalty to the man she loved. In that moment, Camilla turned a deaf ear to all the backlash and criticism and just listened to her heart to prove to Charles that she was not going back.

In the end, with patience, dignity and unwavering devotion, she finally made it.

headline: Maya Jama's company worth more than £4 million after impressive financial growth
subheadline: The impressive figures come after Maya shared her observations about spotting 'red flags' in a relationship
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Maya Jama has demonstrated her business acumen beyond the screen, with her company's fortune soaring to more than £4 million.

According to the DailyMail, The Celebrity Traitors star, 32, has successfully expanded her business empire, increasingly its value by almost £1.4 million in just one year.

Newly published accounts also show her firm had nearly £2.5million in the bank at the end of January this year, plus investments worth almost £1.4million.

READ MORE: Maya Jama shuts down Stormzy comeback talk with cryptic message

Documents lodged at Companies House show her firm, MIJ & Co Entertainment Ltd, was worth more than £4million after its debts were taken into account - up from £2.63million the year before.

The Love Island presenter has been vocal about her business ambitions, with her financial advisers telling her that she could afford to retire by the age of 40.

However, she insisted that she wanted to make a lot more money first.

The impressive figures come as Maya took centre stage in Friday night's final of The Celebrity Traitors, having made it all the way to the last episode as one of just two Traitors left in the game.

READ MORE: Maya Jama joins ‘The Gentlemen' after Meghan Markle rumours denied
