headline: Martin Scorsese reveals why his 'Cleopatra' film never happened
subheadline: Seth Rogen 'ruined' Martin Scorsese’s Cleopatra dream
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Angelina Jolie as Cleopatra under Martin Scorsese’s direction?

Hollywood came surprisingly close to making it happen — until, as the filmmaker jokingly puts it, Seth Rogen ruined everything.

During a conversation with his daughter Francesca at Tribeca on Thursday, October 29, the director, 83, reflected on his unrealised ambition to make a grand Roman epic.

He admitted he had “missed it,” joking that Ridley Scott has now “done [them] all.”

Read More: Martin Scorsese uses AI for filmmaking

But one project still seems to sting: a Cleopatra film with Jolie attached to play the legendary Egyptian queen.

Scorsese revealed that the project fell apart in the aftermath of the 2014 Sony Pictures hack, which followed the studio's plans to release Rogen and Evan Goldberg’s comedy The Interview.

The film mocked North Korea's leadership, prompting a major cyberattack attributed to a North Korean state-sponsored group.

“[Kim Jong Un] got mad and he blew up everybody at Columbia,” Scorsese said. “[It] ruined Cleopatra. Angelina Jolie, we were going. She was Cleopatra VII. It was going to be really wild.”

He then delivered his playful verdict on the whole mess: Seth was the one who “ruined everything.”

“Just because Kim Jong Un didn’t have a sense of humour, you know?” he quipped.

The joke also has a funny connection to The Studio, Rogen’s Apple TV series.

Read More: Martin Scorsese makes a case for 'independent films'

Scorsese appeared as himself in the show, where Rogen’s character also manages to derail the director’s hopes of making a film.

headline: Olivia Rodrigo channels Marie Antoinette for Halloween
subheadline: Olivia Rodrigo stuns fans with Marie Antoinette-inspired look for Unraveled Tour Halloween Showt
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Olivia Rodrigo just brought a royal touch to Halloween.

The 23-year-old pop superstar traded her usual stage looks for an elaborate Marie Antoinette-inspired costume.

The Driver’s License hitmaker dressed as the iconic French queen during her Unraveled Tour stop in Columbus, Ohio, on Friday, October 30.

READ MORE: Olivia Rodrigo roots for My Chemical Romance as chart battle rages

Her elaborate Halloween ensemble gave major 18th-century royal vibes, with her appearance reminding fans of the extravagant world of the Palace of Versailles.

Photos from the concert quickly caught fans' attention, with many praising the singer's gorgeous transformation.

Social media was flooded with enthusiastic reactions. One fan gushed, "She looks so beautiful, this is simply the best Halloween costume she's worn."

Another compared her to a painting at the historic French palace, writing, "She looks like an angel on the walls of Versailles."

A third fan couldn't contain their excitement, commenting, "What the heck omggg I love this."

While Halloween costumes are always a fun part of the season, Rodrigo's royal-inspired appearance gave her Columbus performance an especially memorable twist.

Following the Ohio show, Rodrigo will take her massive global arena tour supporting her third studio album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, to Philadelphia, Atlanta, Orlando, Fort Lauderdale and Nashville in November.

headline: Lily Allen celebrates one year of 'West End Girl' following David Harbour split
subheadline: The 41-year-old British musician turned the pain of her heartbreaking split with David Harbour into art for the album.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lily Allen has shared her happiness and gratitude as she celebrated one year since the release of her comeback album, West End Girl.

The singer took to Instagram to share her feelings, describing her return to music with the record following her divorce from David Harbour has been a 'dream.'

The 41-year-old British musician turned the pain of her heartbreaking split with David Harbour into art for the album.

READ MORE: Lily Allen announces 'West End Girl' documentary after David Harbour split

In the picture, the Tennis hitmaker is seen holding up the album while showing off her incredible figure in a glamorous gold dress.

Lily also debuted her new darker hair and fringe in the snap which was taken during her tour for the album.

She penned in the caption of her post: '1 year of west end girl.. thanks for loving this record, and for coming on this ride with me. What a dream it's been. X.'

This comes after Lily was left 'disappointed' after being forced to cancel her show in New Zealand on Wednesday due to a viral infection.

She is currently embarking on the New Zealand and Australian leg of her global West End Girl tour.

READ MORE: Lily Allen gets candid about her fifth studio album ‘West End Girl'

headline: After Louvre heist and string of thefts, Europe's smaller museums are on guard
subheadline: "If the Louvre was so easy to rob, just imagine a tiny museum in a rural area or a smaller town," says researcher
author: Reuters
article_text:
Two men wearing head torches climbed through a forced-open window at the Fondazione Magnani Rocca museum near Parma on the night of March 22 and calmly lifted artworks by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse from the walls.

Within three minutes, they had passed the works, valued at about €9 million ($10 million), to an accomplice and fled. At the museum's main gate, a fourth man discharged a fire extinguisher when the alarm sounded, distracting the ​custodian.

"Whatever could go wrong, did," said Stefano Roffi, director of the private foundation that runs the museum.

The raid was one of a string of museum thefts in France, Italy and Spain since last year's heist at ‌the Louvre in Paris, raising concerns that criminals are increasingly targeting smaller institutions with fewer resources to protect valuable collections.

"This is where we see the 'Louvre effect'," said Marc Balcells, a Barcelona-based researcher specialising in crimes against cultural heritage. "If the Louvre was so easy to rob, just imagine a tiny museum in a rural area or a smaller town."

Works by Antonello da Messina vanished from a museum in his Sicilian hometown in August, while two Renoirs were stolen from Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera the following month.

In Spain, thieves stole hundreds of historic gold coins from museums in Badajoz and Albacete and made ​off with a Bronze Age treasure in Villena, near Alicante.

A 2024 survey by France's Culture Ministry found only one in four cultural institutions had an emergency and risk-prevention plan, while nearly half lacked video surveillance.

Who checks when the alarm goes off?

A French parliamentary report in May said museums lacked the resources and preparation to adequately protect artworks and artefacts.

In Italy, the challenge is amplified by the way the country's ⁠cultural heritage is spread across hundreds of towns and institutions, a legacy of centuries of fragmented rule.

"That is also what makes our system distinctive: works remain in the places where they were created,” said Antonella Pinna, president of the Italian committee of the ​International Council of Museums. "But we need to make life harder for criminals."

The council worked with Italy's Culture Ministry and the Carabinieri on museum security guidelines published in 2015, but Pinna said technology alone was not enough.

"If an alarm goes off, someone has to ​make sure it is checked," she said.

In a narrow street in the Tuscan town of Sansepolcro, the civic museum displays four works by Renaissance master Piero della Francesca, born just steps away in the 15th century.

The Louvre theft "affected us deeply because cultural heritage is central to Sansepolcro's identity. It is our soul," culture councillor Francesca Mercati told Reuters.

After the Louvre raid, officers from the Carabinieri's cultural heritage protection unit recommended more cameras, longer retention of CCTV footage and tighter controls on bags and bulky clothing.

"We immediately implemented those recommendations," Mercati said.

A vast network to protect

The scale of the challenge ​is daunting.

"The budget is key to winning the war," she said.

France's Culture Ministry announced ‌a 33-point security ⁠plan in July, backed by €30 million over three years for local museums.

Europol said in an August report that museum thefts were becoming more forceful and increasingly focused on precious metals, gemstones and other high-value artefacts.

Unlike gold or jewellery, which can be broken up or melted down, a well-known painting is difficult to turn into quick cash.

Even when works are recovered, museums can face significant costs linked to investigations, recovery efforts and upgraded security.

Insurers are also turning to technology. Beazley is exploring how AI can ​be used to analyse CCTV footage to identify suspicious behaviour in museums and galleries, helping security staff spot threats sooner, said fine art underwriter Dishni Mahendran.

"Ultimately, museums must remain easy to access," Imbert said. "People should be able to enter without having to pass through 50 security checks."

article_html:
Two men wearing head torches climbed through a forced-open window at the Fondazione Magnani Rocca museum near Parma on the night of March 22 and calmly lifted artworks by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse from the walls.

Within three minutes, they had passed the works, valued at about €9 million ($10 million), to an accomplice and fled. At the museum's main gate, a fourth man discharged a fire extinguisher when the alarm sounded, distracting the ​custodian.

"Whatever could go wrong, did," said Stefano Roffi, director of the private foundation that runs the museum.

The raid was one of a string of museum thefts in France, Italy and Spain since last year's heist at ‌the Louvre in Paris, raising concerns that criminals are increasingly targeting smaller institutions with fewer resources to protect valuable collections.

"This is where we see the 'Louvre effect'," said Marc Balcells, a Barcelona-based researcher specialising in crimes against cultural heritage. "If the Louvre was so easy to rob, just imagine a tiny museum in a rural area or a smaller town."

Works by Antonello da Messina vanished from a museum in his Sicilian hometown in August, while two Renoirs were stolen from Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera the following month.

In Spain, thieves stole hundreds of historic gold coins from museums in Badajoz and Albacete and made ​off with a Bronze Age treasure in Villena, near Alicante.

A 2024 survey by France's Culture Ministry found only one in four cultural institutions had an emergency and risk-prevention plan, while nearly half lacked video surveillance.

Who checks when the alarm goes off?

A French parliamentary report in May said museums lacked the resources and preparation to adequately protect artworks and artefacts.

In Italy, the challenge is amplified by the way the country's ⁠cultural heritage is spread across hundreds of towns and institutions, a legacy of centuries of fragmented rule.

"That is also what makes our system distinctive: works remain in the places where they were created,” said Antonella Pinna, president of the Italian committee of the ​International Council of Museums. "But we need to make life harder for criminals."

The council worked with Italy's Culture Ministry and the Carabinieri on museum security guidelines published in 2015, but Pinna said technology alone was not enough.

"If an alarm goes off, someone has to ​make sure it is checked," she said.

In a narrow street in the Tuscan town of Sansepolcro, the civic museum displays four works by Renaissance master Piero della Francesca, born just steps away in the 15th century.

The Louvre theft "affected us deeply because cultural heritage is central to Sansepolcro's identity. It is our soul," culture councillor Francesca Mercati told Reuters.

After the Louvre raid, officers from the Carabinieri's cultural heritage protection unit recommended more cameras, longer retention of CCTV footage and tighter controls on bags and bulky clothing.

"We immediately implemented those recommendations," Mercati said.

Italy has more than 4,400 museums and similar institutions, according to the national statistics agency ISTAT. Spain has about 1,500 museums, while France has more than 1,200 institutions carrying the official "Musees de France" designation, alongside hundreds of smaller collections.
Protecting such a broad network is particularly difficult for smaller institutions that depend on local funding.
Florence Imbert, a Paris-based security consultant for cultural institutions, said 85% of small French museums were run by local authorities with limited financial resources.
"The budget is key to winning the war," she said.
France's Culture Ministry announced ‌a 33-point security ⁠plan in July, backed by €30 million over three years for local museums.
Recent figures suggest concern is warranted. The Carabinieri art squad recorded 17 thefts from Italian museums and galleries in 2025, up from 14 a year earlier.
Europol said in an August report that museum thefts were becoming more forceful and increasingly focused on precious metals, gemstones and other high-value artefacts.
A fast buck?
Unlike gold or jewellery, which can be broken up or melted down, a well-known painting is difficult to turn into quick cash.
Celebrated works such as those by Renoir can rarely be sold openly, Pinna said. Instead, stolen art is more likely to be hidden, used as leverage in ransom attempts or offered privately.
Even when works are recovered, museums can face significant costs linked to investigations, recovery efforts and upgraded security.
The recent thefts have also reignited debate about insurance.

Most major state-backed museums in Western Europe rely on government indemnity schemes rather than ⁠commercial cover, but some institutions have begun reassessing the risks, said Filippo Guerrini-Maraldi, a private wealth and fine art insurance specialist at broker Howden Specialty.
"And for the first time, really, in my 40-year career, I've seen art theft now becoming more of a major, major risk. It was always the minor risk," he said.

Insurers are also turning to technology. Beazley is exploring how AI can be used to analyse CCTV footage to identify suspicious behaviour in museums and galleries, helping security staff spot threats sooner, said fine art underwriter Dishni Mahendran.
Security vs access
For museum directors and cultural officials, the challenge is ⁠how to tighten security without cutting collections off from local communities or diminishing the visitor experience.
"Ultimately, museums must remain easy to access," Imbert said. "People should be able to enter without having to pass through 50 security checks."
Julien Volper, a conservator at Belgium's Africa Museum, said particularly vulnerable treasures should only be displayed when adequate security measures are in place.
"I'm not saying that's the ultimate solution, but it seems better than displaying replicas," he said. "We're not at Disneyland."
In August, the Carabinieri recovered the three artworks stolen from the Parma museum from a cardboard box ⁠hidden in an apartment. Five Moldovan nationals were arrested in connection with the theft.
Investigators said wiretaps indicated the suspects had unsuccessfully tried to find buyers in Eastern Europe and Russia.
The works have since returned to the museum in what Roffi called a "homecoming party".
"The theft triggered an outpouring of solidarity in Italy and abroad," he said. The museum now has round-the-clock guards funded by a local cheese consortium.
"It was seen not simply as a theft from a museum, but as an attack on art as a shared cultural heritage."

headline: King Charles faces major risk after taking bold step to protect monarchy
subheadline: King Charles makes decision for monarchy that no monarch has ever taken before
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles may have gone above and beyond to show how that he may be different from his predecessors, but it just is “not good enough” for the history books.

According to royal expert Russell Myers, the monarch will have a confront a brutal reality check even if the Caribbean tour turns out to be a ‘successful one.

The King was received warmly in The Bahamas and Guyana, even though there was a small number of anti-monarchy protestors.

READ MORE: Buckingham Palace shares update as King holds meeting after urgent appeal

Russell argued that even though Charles acknowledged the “mistakes of the past, king are rarely judged on intentions alone. The UK government has made it clear that there would be no apology and reparations.

They fear that “a legal precedent that could open the floodgates for former colonies around the world”. And the King acts on the advice of his ministers and the Government.

As for the most hopeful note for Charles, “there is a path between apology and silence, and it is one he has walked for years” which means that the Commonwealth leaders will discuss the legacy of slavery in Antigua next week.

However, moves are already being made and the “ground is shifting beneath him”.

Barbados left the monarchy in 2021 and Jamaica is pushing towards becoming a republic.

Hence, if Chogm ends with “warm words and little else, the danger is that his reign in the Caribbean will be remembered not for the moments of reflection, but for the apology that never came”.

headline: Prince Harry's biggest fear about William laid bare
subheadline: Prince William accuseed of changing King Charles mind amid Harry's emotional plea
author: Shehzad Hameed
article_text:
Prince Harry allegedly believes that his elder brother, Prince William, is the biggest hurdle in his return to the royal fold as he makes a desperate plea to return to his father and other senior royals.

The Duke is said to be 'worried' that the future King is allegedly turning the monarch against him.

A source revealed that the Duke is convinced his brother would love nothing more than to see him cut out completely.

READ MORE: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle fleeing back to US after failed UK test: 'Devastated'

Harry, according to a new claim, believes: "William is slowly turning his own father against him."

Previously, royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Page Six that William's circle believes "money and inheritance" are part of the reason behind the Sussexes' push to return to the UK.

However, King Charles' youngest son insists that money has nothing to do with this push. It's all about peace, as he genuinely does want a relationship with Charles.

The Sussexes reportedly have enormous expenses and there is always pressure to keep bringing money in.

While Harry, who has lived a life of incredible privilege compared to most, now feels immense pressure when it comes to his finances and future, William is looking at the bigger picture.

On the other hand, William does not want any new drama in the family. Focused on his future reign, he wants only trusted people around him, not those who struggle to keep things private and whose actions continue to linger in his thoughts as a fear.

READ MORE: Queen Camilla's unexpected gesture with powerful message: Details inside

headline: Fatal shooting at Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield leaves 1 dead, 6 injured
subheadline: Fairfield police chief said the shooting took place inside the Spirit Halloween store at Solano Town Centre mall at 8:30 p.m. on Friday
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A fatal shooting incident at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield has left one dead and 6 injured on Friday night.

According to the Fairfield police officials, deputies responded to a shooting inside the Solano Town Centre mall at the Spirit Halloween store at 8:30 p.m.

The Fairfield Police Department Chief, Dan Marshall, held a news conference about the incident at the Solano Town Centre mall.

Marshall confirmed the suspect opened fire in a mall, which left one dead while wounding six others, who were taken to the hospital, and three of them are said to be in critical condition.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with the families of the victims of this heartbreaking incident,” he said, adding that all of the victims had been taken to a nearby hospital.

The suspect has so far not been identified amid the ongoing investigation.

Suisun City police said they assisted the primary agency by providing mutual aid on multiple victims and officers were searching for a suspect.

California Highway Patrol said it was assisting police with traffic control and clearing buildings.

The Fairfield police have provided emergency contact details for general public with anyone who details can reach out to the department at 707-428-7600.

headline: PM Shehbaz seeks suspension of long-term projects in KP, urges short-term steps
subheadline: PML-N had played important role in promoting democratic traditions in province, says prime minister
author: Web Desk
article_text:
PM Shehbaz says KP people suffered for 13 years under PTI govt.
Pakistan bore immense losses in fight against terrorism: PM.
PM says governor's rule was necessary to protect people, country.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has called for prioritising short-term development initiatives over long-term projects in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), stressing the need for immediate measures to provide relief to the people of the province.

"If you take small steps to improve law and order, build a school, and ensure medicines reach hospitals, people who have been deprived for 13 years will pray for you," he said, criticising the Imran Khan-founded Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) more than a decade in power in the province.

"Long-term projects should be suspended," he added.

The premier made these remarks while addressing a Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) KP parliamentary party meeting on Saturday.

He also stressed the need to prioritise short-term measures to provide immediate relief to the people of the province, which has been under the governor's rule since the federal government imposed it on October 11.

The PML-N-led federal government imposed governor’s rule and emergency in the province on October 11 — effectively ending the provincial government’s powers.

At the time, the Centre had alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.

Under the new arrangement, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi — a leader of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) — exercises the provincial government's functions on behalf of the federation with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council, while Parliament exercises the provincial assembly's legislative powers.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz said that the PML-N had played an important role in promoting democratic traditions in the province.

Recalling the 2013 general elections, the prime minister said that former prime minister Nawaz Sharif had allowed the majority party in KP to form the provincial government.

However, PM Shehbaz questioned the performance of the PTI government, which he said had remained in power in the province for the past 13 years.

"They made slogans and delivered speeches, but what did they actually achieve?" he asked, adding that the party had made numerous claims about development projects.

The prime minister also questioned the province's healthcare facilities, arrangements for medicines and treatment, and measures taken to eliminate corruption.

He further raised questions about the transparency of public funds and the utilisation of resources during the PTI's tenure.

Security situation

The prime minister also highlighted the sacrifices made by KP's people in the fight against terrorism.

He said the people of the province, police personnel, armed forces and political leaders had rendered unparalleled sacrifices in the war against militancy.

Pakistan had suffered enormous human and economic losses in the fight against terrorism, he added.

PM Shehbaz said terrorism had been completely eliminated from KP during 2017-18 through collective efforts by the nation and state institutions under Nawaz's leadership.

The prime minister alleged that terrorists were brought back from Afghanistan and resettled in 2019 and 2020, adding that the resurgence of terrorism had caused significant damage to the country.

He said the government had invited political stakeholders to join efforts against terrorism, as had been done in the past, but its appeals had not been heeded.

'Necessary step'

Defending the decision to impose governor's rule and emergency measures in KP, the prime minister said the federal government had attempted to resolve differences through negotiations.

He said committees comprising representatives of the PPP and PML-N had held discussions for 48 hours with the PTI.

According to PM Shehbaz, Centre waited for approval of a draft agreed during the negotiations with the opposition, but the approval never came.

The premier said that the decision had become necessary to protect the people, the country, the economy and society.

article_html:
• PM Shehbaz says KP people suffered for 13 years under PTI govt.
  • Pakistan bore immense losses in fight against terrorism: PM.
  • PM says governor's rule was necessary to protect people, country.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has called for prioritising short-term development initiatives over long-term projects in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), stressing the need for immediate measures to provide relief to the people of the province.

"If you take small steps to improve law and order, build a school, and ensure medicines reach hospitals, people who have been deprived for 13 years will pray for you," he said, criticising the Imran Khan-founded Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) more than a decade in power in the province.

"Long-term projects should be suspended," he added.

The premier made these remarks while addressing a Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) KP parliamentary party meeting on Saturday.

He also stressed the need to prioritise short-term measures to provide immediate relief to the people of the province, which has been under the governor's rule since the federal government imposed it on October 11.

The PML-N-led federal government imposed governor’s rule and emergency in the province on October 11 — effectively ending the provincial government’s powers.

At the time, the Centre had alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.

Under the new arrangement, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi — a leader of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) — exercises the provincial government's functions on behalf of the federation with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council, while Parliament exercises the provincial assembly's legislative powers.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz said that the PML-N had played an important role in promoting democratic traditions in the province.

Recalling the 2013 general elections, the prime minister said that former prime minister Nawaz Sharif had allowed the majority party in KP to form the provincial government.

However, PM Shehbaz questioned the performance of the PTI government, which he said had remained in power in the province for the past 13 years.

"They made slogans and delivered speeches, but what did they actually achieve?" he asked, adding that the party had made numerous claims about development projects.

The prime minister also questioned the province's healthcare facilities, arrangements for medicines and treatment, and measures taken to eliminate corruption.

He further raised questions about the transparency of public funds and the utilisation of resources during the PTI's tenure.

Security situation

The prime minister also highlighted the sacrifices made by KP's people in the fight against terrorism.

He said the people of the province, police personnel, armed forces and political leaders had rendered unparalleled sacrifices in the war against militancy.

Pakistan had suffered enormous human and economic losses in the fight against terrorism, he added.

PM Shehbaz said terrorism had been completely eliminated from KP during 2017-18 through collective efforts by the nation and state institutions under Nawaz's leadership.

The prime minister alleged that terrorists were brought back from Afghanistan and resettled in 2019 and 2020, adding that the resurgence of terrorism had caused significant damage to the country.

He said the government had invited political stakeholders to join efforts against terrorism, as had been done in the past, but its appeals had not been heeded.

'Necessary step'

Defending the decision to impose governor's rule and emergency measures in KP, the prime minister said the federal government had attempted to resolve differences through negotiations.

He said committees comprising representatives of the PPP and PML-N had held discussions for 48 hours with the PTI.

According to PM Shehbaz, Centre waited for approval of a draft agreed during the negotiations with the opposition, but the approval never came.

The premier said that the decision had become necessary to protect the people, the country, the economy and society.

"Had a timely decision not been taken, the province could have suffered further damage," the prime minister said.

He reiterated that the PML-N would continue its efforts for the development, prosperity and public welfare of KP.

headline: Edo shares first message after Beatrice's outing with Sarah Ferguson
subheadline: Princess Beatrice's husband Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi makes feelings clear after wife takes u-turn on decision
author: A. Akmal
article_text:
Princess Beatrice’s husband, Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi, emerged on the scene just two days after his wife took a decisive step for the family.

It was believed that Beatrice and her sister Princess Eugenie not only be keeping a distance from their parents but also from each other as their royal statuses hung in balance.

The sisters seem to have taken a major U-turn in their plans as they were spotted with their mother Sarah Ferguson in UK after months of no public appearances together.

READ MORE: Sarah Ferguson smiles in first UK outing with Beatrice, Eugenie

This was a surprise outing and happened while King Charles is carrying out his high-stakes Caribbean tour.

Beatrice’s husband, Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi, who has been pouring in efforts into a slew of his luxury property development projects seems to have made his feelings clear on the matter: he will stay out of it.

The Banda founder shared an update after the outing, keeping the highlight on his work, but silently supporting his wife.

“Oxblood. That perfect point between burgundy, brown and red. Warm, sophisticated and endlessly seductive. A colour I will never tire of.”

There had been silence over his social media page for more than a week and this update shows that Edo could be using his platform to divert any extra attention away at a crucial time like this.

Edo and Beatrice have been subject to separation rumours for months prior to this, with sources citing that the couple had been facing issues due to Andrew and Fergie’s scandal.

They have since dismissed the rumours after making appearances together.

READ MORE: Beatrice, Eugenie forced to take heartbreaking step amid Andrew bombshell

headline: S Club send fans into frenzy with major reunion announcement
subheadline: There is also speculation that the pop band could release new music for the first time after 28 years
author: Web Desk
article_text:
S Club have set the internet into a frenzy after announcing their reunion for a huge UK tour next year.

Bradley Mclntosh, 45, Rachel Stevens, 48, Jon Lee, 44, Tina Barrett, 50, and Jo O’Meara, 47, will come together to perform a number of shows across the country.

There is also speculation that the pop band could release new music for the first time after 28 years.

Announcing the news, S Club said: 'We can’t wait to get back out on tour, see you all and celebrate the songs, memories and moments we’ve shared together over the years. It’s going to be one BIG party, and we want you all to be part of it!'

READ MORE: Rachel Stevens addresses S Club 7 reunion: 'one million percent up for it’

Hannah Spearritt will not take part in the UK tour, after she pulled out from their 25th anniversary tour plans in 2023 following bandmate Paul Cattermole's tragic death.

The five-piece joined Boyzone as special guests at London's Emirates Stadium in June.

headline: Jennifer Lawrence honest take on post-baby body changes
subheadline: Jennifer Lawrence's breast lift plans spark controversy across the internet
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jennifer Lawrence is not interested in pretending motherhood means putting her own confidence on the back burner.

The actress has sparked a conversation about post-pregnancy body changes after revealing that she wants to get a breast lift.

Speaking to The Cut, Lawrence explained that the decision comes down to something simple: she still wants to feel sexy as a mother.

Read More: Jennifer Lawrence rules out her probablity of returning to 'X-Men'

She also joked about wanting to turn up at her child’s school looking like a woman who has her life together — even when she has only just rolled out of bed. Relatable? Absolutely.

For the No Hard Feelings star, the idea isn't about setting a beauty standard for other mothers.

It's a personal choice, and one that highlights how becoming a parent doesn't mean giving up the parts of yourself that existed before children.

Women can adore motherhood and still want to feel attractive, confident and comfortable in their changing bodies.

The two things aren't mutually exclusive.

Lawrence has previously been candid about speculation surrounding her appearance.

In a 2023 interview with Kylie Jenner for Interview, she denied undergoing eye surgery, explaining that makeup and the natural loss of facial fat with age could account for the changes people had noticed.

This time, however, she's talking about a procedure she is genuinely considering, rather than responding to online rumours.

Read More: Jennifer Lawrence confirms cosmetic surgery after two kids

Her comments also raise a bigger question: why are mothers so often expected to accept every physical change without admitting they might want to change something?

headline: 'Dune 3' stars deliver exciting news for fans ahead of movie release
subheadline: 'Dune' fans get double treat as first two movies return to IMAX with an exclusive 'Dune 3' sneak peek
author: Javeria Shahid
article_text:
Dune fans have a major reason to celebrate as the stars of the highly anticipated third installment have joined forces to deliver some exciting news.

Fulfilling fans’ demand, the Dune team has decided to give audiences a chance to revisit Arrakis on the big screen while offering an exclusive glimpse of what's coming next.

The official movie's Instagram account announced that Dune and Dune: Part Two are returning to IMAX theaters for a limited one-week engagement starting November 13.

READ MORE: Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya tease end of epic journey in new ‘Dune' video

And that's not all! Moviegoers will also get to witness an exclusive sneak peek of Dune: Part Three, making the special theatrical re-release an even bigger treat for fans eagerly awaiting the next chapter.

The announcement came with a hilarious video featuring Zendaya, Timothée Chalamet, Florence Pugh, Robert Pattinson, Jason Momoa and Anya Taylor-Joy.

Kicking things off, Tom Holland’s wife told fans, "Well, lucky you guys, because we are releasing..." before breaking into a playful, swaying delivery of the announcement about bringing the first two films back for audiences to watch.

Meanwhile, Pugh and Chalamet hilariously tried to squeeze themselves into the camera frame, while the other stars struggled to contain their laughter at Zendaya's amusing delivery.

The video was a response to a fan request attached to the clip, which read, "They should re-release Dune and Dune 2 before Dune 3 comes out."

The Dune team heard them as fans are getting exactly the kind of cinematic treat they were hoping for.

READ MORE: ‘Dune' fans get emotional over Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya's new video

READ MORE: Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya tease end of epic journey in new ‘Dune' video

And that's not all! Moviegoers will also get to witness an exclusive sneak peek of Dune: Part Three, making the special theatrical re-release an even bigger treat for fans eagerly awaiting the next chapter.
The announcement came with a hilarious video featuring Zendaya, Timothée Chalamet, Florence Pugh, Robert Pattinson, Jason Momoa and Anya Taylor-Joy.

Kicking things off, Tom Holland’s wife told fans, "Well, lucky you guys, because we are releasing..." before breaking into a playful, swaying delivery of the announcement about bringing the first two films back for audiences to watch.
Meanwhile, Pugh and Chalamet hilariously tried to squeeze themselves into the camera frame, while the other stars struggled to contain their laughter at Zendaya's amusing delivery.
The video was a response to a fan request attached to the clip, which read, "They should re-release Dune and Dune 2 before Dune 3 comes out."
The Dune team heard them as fans are getting exactly the kind of cinematic treat they were hoping for.

headline: Prince Edward, Duchess Sophie receive good news about Lady Louise new role
subheadline: Lady Louise makes King Charles proud after taking on secret position for the royals
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh had just concluded their visit to Finland at the behest of the Buckingham Palace, proving their dedication to work and duty.

And, their 22-year-old daughter, who graduated from university over the summer, has been doing the same, as a royal insider shares rare details about the King’s niece.

Lady Louise had been gradually earning praise and popularity with her hard work, which it seems, she has taken after her parents.

READ MORE: Duchess Sophie's daughter takes after mum in secret role for King Charles

Lady Louise had been gradually earning praise and popularity with her hard work, which it seems, she has taken after her parents.

The young royal is currently focussed on gaining experience in her gap year. According to royal photographer James Whatling, who has worked alongside the royals for many years, Louise had gained “extra confidence”.

“One thing that strikes me about her is that she may be quiet and you don’t see a lot of her, but I think underneath all that there’s a steely determination,” he told HELLO!.

“You see her with the horses, and she commands them. She’s fearless. It’s a tricky thing to do.”

This comes after it was revealed that Louise, who is 18th in line to the throne, had quietly taken on a position at Charles’s Scottish estate for several weeks.

She had taken on the duty of cooking for the guests renting the luxury lodges. Sources close to the Edinburghs had shared that just like Sophie, Louise is also a talented cook.

headline: Stephen Curry drops Doncic with viral move in 25-point comeback win in NBA Cup
subheadline: The Warriors registered three straight wins, opening the 2026-27 season 0-3 for the first time after drafting Stephen Curry
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Luka Doncic was ready to make a headline in the Los Angeles Lakers’ NBA Cup opening game, but only for one quarter on Friday, October 30, 2026.

The Los Angeles Lakers opened the scoring with a 40-15 run that stretched into the second quarter, with the Golden State Warriors appearing to be a fading team.

Doncic, who appeared locked in, scored 21 points, 5 assists, 3 rebounds and 1 steal in the first quarter alone.

But Warriors made a stunning comeback in the second quarter with a 38-15 lead to tie the game at halftime and storm back from a 25-point lead and seal the win with 112-95.

However, despite the 25-point comeback, the highlight of the game was the viral moment when Stephen Curry dropped Lakers guard Doncic in the third quarter before attempting a 3-pointer to narrow the deficit to six points.

Curry scored 31 points on 11-of-23 shooting attempts (8-of-14 from 3-point range) plus 6 assists and 4 rebounds.

While Doncic finished the game with 37 points on 12-of-27 shooting attempts, 7 rebounds and 5 assists.

The Warriors have registered three straight wins, opening the 2026-27 season 0-3 for the first time after drafting Curry.

The win, along with the record margin of victory, provides them a key advantage in NBA Cup play, where they are grouped with the Lakers, San Antonio Spurs, Portland Trail Blazers and Sacramento Kings.

headline: Buckingham Palace receives bombshell update form Met Police
subheadline: King Charles' office receives a shocking news amid crisis
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles' office has received a shocking update on the royal family's annual event's security.

The Metropolitan Police will reportedly reduce the number of officers assigned to Trooping the Colour as a private firm takes over major royal events in London.

The force has removed what sources told the Telegraph to be "the vast majority" of its policing provision for the King's birthday parade, along with gun salutes and the Changing of the Guard.

READ MORE: Prince Harry's biggest fear about William laid bare

The revised arrangements, due to come into effect in Novnember, only a "minimal" police presence will remain at these events. The police will hand most security duties to a private contractor instead.

The sweeping reductions have been driven by budgetary constraints and growing pressure to redirect officers towards front-line neighbourhood policing.

While Met sources maintained the force would still back "nationally significant events," a defence source disputed this, telling the publication: "They are not supporting Trooping the Colour in the same way, nor many other events."

Over the past year, an estimated 17,800 officers were deployed to support military ceremonial duties, eportedly costing the Met roughly £10.6million.

The spokesman added: "Against a backdrop of financial cuts and increased demand, we had to make difficult decisions about what to prioritise to protect Londoners and over recent months have engaged with the Ministry of Defence around proposed changes to how we support military ceremonial events."

READ MORE: Queen Camilla's unexpected gesture with powerful message: Details inside

headline: Disney's live-action ‘Tangled' gets major update
subheadline: Tangled Screenwriter Michael Montemayor posts behind-the-scenes photos from the table read
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Disney's live-action Tangled fans are one step closer to seeing Rapunzel and Flynn Rider return to the big screen.

Screenwriter Michael "Mikey" Montemayor has celebrated the movie's wrap by sharing a behind-the-scenes glimpse of the highly anticipated reimagining.

Taking to Instagram on Friday, October 30, he announced, "That's a wrap on Tangled!!”

READ MORE: Disney's live-action 'Tangled' locks in its Mother Gothel

“Truly a dream come true getting to see this movie come to life!" the screenwriter added, while also reflecting on his journey.

Montemayor revealed that he had been writing movies since he was 19 and described the opportunity to work with Disney on four projects this year as "a miracle in the making."

His announcement came with a carousel, beginning with an image of a Tangled script. Another picture showed him posing at the movie's table read, while the remaining snapshots offered additional glimpses of his experience working on the Disney project.

He ended his post by teasing, "More to come soon!"

For the unversed, Montemayor is part of the writing team behind Disney's upcoming live-action adaptation of the beloved 2010 animated classic.

He joined Jennifer Kaytin Robinson as a co-writer, contributing to the screenplay revisions for the new adaptation. The original animated film was written by Dan Fogelman.

The update has already sparked excitement among fans, who flooded the comments with congratulatory messages.

"Congratsss really excited to see it," one fan wrote, while another exclaimed, "GIVE IT TO ME ASAP BABY." A third fan shared their enthusiasm, declaring, "The only live action I'm excited for!!!"

Disney's live-action Tangled is currently scheduled to hit theaters on March 31, 2028, giving fans plenty of reason to look forward to Rapunzel's next big-screen adventure.

READ MORE: Milo Manheim tapped for lead role in ‘Tangled' live-action movie

headline: Claudia Winkleman breaks silence on picking Richard E Grant
subheadline: The actor, 69, was the first person to be banished in the current series of the BBC show
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Claudia Winkleman has opened up about her decision to pick Richard E Grant as a Traitor after he made one of the biggest gaffes in the show's history.

The host, 54, appeared on The Celebrity Traitors spin-off show Uncloaked on Friday following the grand finale.

During the show, Claudia was asked by Ed Gamble why she had picked Richard and what she made of the moment where he confessed to being a Traitor.

Claudia said: 'We couldn't not pick him. If you'd have been in that gold chat. It was what he wanted. I don't know if you've ever faced a three-year-old who really wants an ice-cream?

READ MORE: ‘Traitors' icon Claudia Winkleman makes major career move

'The answer is: "yes, Richard. I can't not give this to you. He really wanted to be a Traitor and he was excellent - at the beginning.

'He was even excellent when he said: "I am a Traitor". We've never had that before. I dropped my jacket potato. That was huge. I dropped it next to the clothing rail, every single item was sent back with flecks of tuna.'

The actor, 69, was the first person to be banished in the current series of the BBC show after he revealed he was a Traitor when asked by comedian Joe Lycett, 38.

Viewers watched on Friday as Faithfuls Romesh Ranganathan, 48, and Sebastian Croft, 24, were crowned the winners following a nail-biting final.

headline: San Diego County street gangs targeted in major drug trafficking operation
subheadline: The operation, led by hundreds of FBI agents alongside federal, state and local law enforcement agencies, seized drugs, firearms, ammunition and cash during the operation
author: Web Desk
article_text:
U.S. federal authorities have charged 42 alleged members and their associates after a major drug trafficking sweep against San Diego street gangs.

The probe involved methamphetamine, fentanyl and suspected ties to Mexican drug cartels.

The FBI agents raided a Lemon Grove house on an early Wednesday morning, and they were shot by one of the accused gang members.

Images that were released to the media showing weapons and wrapped blocks of drugs confiscated at multiple locations around the county.

Sales and distribution reportedly happened in communities from Oceanside and Escondido to El Cajon and Chula Vista.

34 of the suspects are already in federal custody.

Among those arrested was John Marquez, a high-ranking member of the Poway gang, who is accused of running cross-border drug distribution operations.

The authorities are still going after seven additional defendants.

The operation, led by hundreds of FBI agents alongside federal, state and local law enforcement agencies, seized drugs, firearms, ammunition and cash during the operation and throughout the probe.

The crackdown followed a two-year investigation into the Poway-based gang with alleged links to the Mexican cartels.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jill Streja and Shivanjali A. Sewak.

The 42 defendants face charges outlined in four federal grand jury indictments.

headline: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact, says foreign minister
subheadline: "Discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance," says Asaad al-Shaibani
author: AFP
article_text:
Saudi Arabia is the key backer of Syria's incumbent government.
Kingdom signs defence agreement with Pakistan and Turkiye.
UK said it would deploy fighter jets to help KSA against attacks.

Syria's top diplomat on Saturday said Damascus is considering whether to join the Nato-style Makkah defence alliance that binds Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

Saudi Arabia, under fire from Yemen's Houthis, is a key backer of Syria's government that came to power after the fall of former strongman Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

"Discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance," Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain.

Saudi Arabia has been rallying support against escalating Houthi attacks, including a major strike that closed Riyadh's international airport for two weeks this month.

In August, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the defence pact in Makkah, which states an attack on one country is to be considered an attack on all three.

Earlier this month, French President Emmanuel Macron made a surprise visit to Riyadh and said France had sent troops to help shield a key Saudi oil terminal from Houthi attacks.

Also in October, the UK government announced it would deploy British fighter planes to help Saudi Arabia against the attacks.

The United States on Friday confirmed that it had ordered non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia, effective October 23, citing security risks from Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure.

The US embassy in Riyadh warned American citizens of possible further attacks, airspace closures, flight cancellations and other travel disruptions.

The fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government has intensified in recent weeks, opening another volatile front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran.

A truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition collapsed in July. The group subsequently declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, attacked Saudi vessels and the East-West pipeline, and seized Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Reuters.

Syria's top diplomat on Saturday said Damascus is considering whether to join the Nato-style Makkah defence alliance that binds Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

Saudi Arabia, under fire from Yemen's Houthis, is a key backer of Syria's government that came to power after the fall of former strongman Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

"Discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance," Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain.

Saudi Arabia has been rallying support against escalating Houthi attacks, including a major strike that closed Riyadh's international airport for two weeks this month.

In August, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the defence pact in Makkah, which states an attack on one country is to be considered an attack on all three.

Earlier this month, French President Emmanuel Macron made a surprise visit to Riyadh and said France had sent troops to help shield a key Saudi oil terminal from Houthi attacks.

Also in October, the UK government announced it would deploy British fighter planes to help Saudi Arabia against the attacks.

The United States on Friday confirmed that it had ordered non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia, effective October 23, citing security risks from Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure.

The US embassy in Riyadh warned American citizens of possible further attacks, airspace closures, flight cancellations and other travel disruptions.

The fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government has intensified in recent weeks, opening another volatile front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran.

A truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition collapsed in July. The group subsequently declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, attacked Saudi vessels and the East-West pipeline, and seized Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Reuters.

headline: Kensington Palace shares rare treat of William and Kate's bundle of joy
subheadline: Kate Middleton's throwback Halloween outing with George and Charlotte at local supermarket
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have delighted royal fans with a rare Halloween surprise, sharing a sweet photograph of Prince Louis from his toddler years.

Posted on October 31, the picture shows the young prince at just one year old, leaning towards a large orange pumpkin.

Dressed in a navy blue hooded jacket and red boots, Louis rests both hands on the pumpkin, looking every bit the curious little boy.

Read More: Prince William, Kate dragged into Meghan's controversy

The photograph was taken by his mother, Catherine in 2019. Now eight years old, the young royal has grown up considerably since the picture was captured, making the unexpected throwback all the more special.

Alongside the picture, the royal couple shared a simple Halloween greeting, writing: “Happy Halloween!” They also credited Catherine as the photographer.

Halloween messages from the Prince and Princess of Wales are uncommon on their official social media accounts, making this year's post a welcome surprise for their followers.

The Wales family has, however, been known to enjoy the occasion privately.

In October 2019, Kate was spotted browsing spooky costumes at a Sainsbury's supermarket near the family's Anmer Hall home, with Prince George and Princess Charlotte.

Read More: Kate Middleton sends heartfelt message to George

headline: Daisy May Cooper stuns fans with incredible 10 stone weight loss
subheadline: Daisy's remarkable transformation was on display as she promoted her new book on The One Show on Friday
author: Web Desk
article_text:
She is certainly looking gorgeous!

Daisy May Cooper has shocked fans with her impressive weight loss transformation after shedding 10-stone.

Her remarkable transformation was on display as she promoted her new book on The One Show on Friday.

The This Country star, 40, is said to have lost a significant amount of weight by following a low-carb diet, dropping from a dress size 24 to a size 10.

READ MORE: Robert Aramayo shocks BAFTA crowd with Best Actor win

Daisy showed off her new slim figure in a pinafore dress as she appeared on the BBC show alongside presenter Sarah Greene.

It comes after Daisy revealed that she was trolled and shamed after losing so much weight and panicked that her change in appearance would result in her getting fewer roles.

One of her more celebrated achievements came in 2018, when she won the BAFTA TV Award for Best Female Comedy Performance for her portrayal of Kerry Mucklowe in the BBC Three series This Country.

headline: Meghan Markle's UK dream turns into total humiliation with fresh blow
subheadline: The Duchess of Sussex is facing a full-blown crisis as sales of brand fall to zero
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle has been hit with a third blow in a row since touching down in Britain with Prince Harry and their two children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet in August, turning what was meant to be a triumphant homecoming into total humiliation.

The Duchess of Sussex's lifestyle empire is facing a full-blown crisis, with sales falling to zero after the horrifying allegations involving her father Thomas Markle.

The upsetting allegations and investigation have sent shockwaves through the family and raised deeply disturbing questions about what happened, who knew what, and when.

READ MORE: Meghan Markle, Prince Harry make alliance with Sarah Ferguson?

For Meghan, the fallout seems to be a commercial disaster. Her business is built around selling picture-perfect domestic bliss, family values and an aspirational lifestyle.

The lates blow seems to be a nightmare as consumers are talking about the allegations surrounding her own family instead of talking about her products.

“Sales were already terrible when the allegations first surfaced. Now they’ve fallen to zero,” a source revealed to Rob Shuter.

“This is about something far more serious than a business setback. These are deeply disturbing allegations, and people are horrified. Nobody wants to be sold a fantasy of family happiness while questions this serious remain unanswered.”

“Meghan cannot simply turn the page and pretend this isn’t happening. The allegations are extremely serious, and people want answers. Her lifestyle brand is now caught in the middle of a family scandal that refuses to go away,” the source adds.

Questions are also being raised about what Meghan knew, when she knew it, and why the controversy is only now receiving such public attention.

For the Duchess, the challenge is enormous. She is said to be under extraordinary pressure.

READ MORE: Prince Harry's biggest fear about William laid bare

headline: Abuse survivors to press Church on accountability during pope's trip to South America
subheadline: Survivors from several countries want Pope Leo to introduce stronger rules, investigate Church leaders to support victims
author: Reuters
article_text:
As Pope Leo prepares to return to South America, Peruvian abuse survivor Pedro Salinas sees reason for both hope and unease in the pope’s record confronting clerical abuse.

For a decade, Salinas watched as the Catholic Church investigated Sodalitium Christianae Vitae, the Peru-founded Catholic ​community he helped expose. Then, in the final days of Pope Francis' papacy last year, the Vatican dissolved the group and its branches.

"What was achieved, nobody, absolutely nobody, could even have imagined. It was inconceivable. But ‌it happened," said Salinas, 63, a journalist and former member whose reporting helped expose allegations of sexual, physical and psychological abuse inside the group.

Robert Prevost, as Leo was known when he was a bishop in Peru and later a Vatican cardinal, quietly worked with survivors and advocates, Salinas said, attending meetings, gathering information and communicating by WhatsApp and email.

"Without him, the needle didn't move," Salinas said.

The first US-born pope will travel through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru November 6 to 17, ending with six days in Peru, where he arrived as a missionary in the 1980s and later became a citizen and served ​as bishop of Chiclayo. The Vatican said he will meet clergy abuse survivors there, as he has done on other recent trips.

Survivors say they wonder whether Leo's approach in Peru, which they credit with helping bring about the rare step of ​dissolving a Catholic community, can translate into broader change across a Church where they say accountability is uneven.

“What is lacking are bishops everywhere in the world committed to this issue," Salinas said.

Peru ⁠is preparing for a tourism bonanza during Leo's visit. José Enrique Escardó, 56, president of a Peruvian survivors network, views the excitement from a different perspective.

While Escardó acknowledged that some survivors credit Leo with helping dissolve Sodalitium, he said the Church's actions have not ​delivered sufficient justice, accountability, or reparations.

“Survivors have grown tired of being told things, of being promised things, but nothing being done,” Escardó said. “We feel more abandoned. We feel deceived.”

He wants survivors to become involved in shaping Church policy and wants reparations to include psychological ​care and education.

The Vatican did not respond to a request for comment for this story.

'Tip of the iceberg'

Francis, the first Latin American pope, left a complicated legacy, survivors say. Juan Carlos Cruz, the survivor whose case became central to Francis' 2018 reckoning with abuse in Chile, credits Francis with changes including revisions to canon law, removal of the pontifical secret — the Church's highest level of confidentiality — surrounding abuse cases and Vos Estis Lux Mundi, a Vatican framework for bishops accused of abuse or cover-up.

"We're still at the tip of the iceberg," said Cruz, whom Francis appointed in 2021 to the Pontifical Commission ​for the Protection of Minors. "The commission has been working for years on universal safeguarding guidelines and those standards need to be applied around the world."

Anne Barrett Doyle, co-director of the watchdog group BishopAccountability.org, which tracks Catholic Church abuse allegations worldwide, called Vos Estis ​the most significant action Francis took on abuse. But she said the Vatican rarely makes clear whether an accused bishop's resignation represents punishment.

“The public is left in the dark,” she said.

Barrett Doyle said the Vatican has not released global disciplinary data comparable with figures it provided to a ‌United Nations committee ⁠in 2014. Her group relies on public records, media reports and investigations by prosecutors, governments and commissions to track cases.

She wants Leo to make permanent removal from ministry the universal rule for priests found under canon law to have sexually abused children, extending worldwide a policy adopted by US bishops in 2002.

"To say that no child molesters should be out to practice as priests is just such a no-brainer," she said. “It's a step that Leo could take now.”

Vatican officials have previously cited the difficulty of creating a single abuse reporting law across all countries and argued that removing priests can put them beyond Church supervision.

Angela Walker, executive director of the US-based Survivors Network of those Abused by Priests, said survivors increasingly turn to civil authorities because of the Church's "incredible failure" to police itself.

"There needs to ​be more transparency, more openness, and more accountability," she said. "I ​will believe it when I see it."

Survivors' long wait

In Mexico, ⁠survivors pressed the Vatican on clerical abuse decades before it became a defining crisis across Latin America. Among the most notorious cases was that of Marcial Maciel, the Mexican priest who founded the Legion of Christ order and whose accusers took allegations to the Vatican in the 1990s. The Vatican ordered Maciel in 2006 to withdraw from public ministry. He died in 2008, without ever facing ​his accusers.

The scale of his abuse became clearer after his death. In 2019, the Legion reported that Maciel had abused at least 60 minors, among 175 instances of child abuse the order ​documented involving 33 priests over eight ⁠decades.

José de Jesús Barba Martin, 87, alleged Maciel abused him when he was studying for the priesthood in the 1950s. He recalled survivors struggling to be heard by Church and state authorities in the late 1990s and said an appeal he sent Pope John Paul II went unanswered.

Decades later, that experience has left him with little expectation that another appeal to Rome would bring change.

“The Church is made up of two types of men: good and bad, courageous and cowardly," he said. "It will take a long time, and the issue will not be addressed ⁠under this pope ​nor the next."

Alberto Athié, 72, a former Mexican priest who pursued clerical abuse cases from inside the Church before leaving the priesthood in 2003, sees Leo's ​visit as another opportunity to push for transparency.

“I do have hope,” he said. “But my hope fades just the same ... Things have to be fixed within the Church."

Abuse survivor Sebastian Cuattromo said the Argentine Church should have been “at the international forefront” of confronting abuse under Argentine Pope Francis, but fell short of what he had ​hoped to see.

"There is a major outstanding debt," Cuattromo said.

Argentina's Episcopal Conference declined to comment.

He wants survivors to become involved in shaping Church policy and wants reparations to include psychological care and education.
The Vatican did not respond to a request for comment for this story.
'Tip of the iceberg'

Francis, the first Latin American pope, left a complicated legacy, survivors say. Juan Carlos Cruz, the survivor whose case became central to Francis' 2018 reckoning with abuse in Chile, credits Francis with changes including revisions to canon law, removal of the pontifical secret — the Church's highest level of confidentiality — surrounding abuse cases and Vos Estis Lux Mundi, a Vatican framework for bishops accused of abuse or cover-up.

"We're still at the tip of the iceberg," said Cruz, whom Francis appointed in 2021 to the Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors. "The commission has been working for years on universal safeguarding guidelines and those standards need to be applied around the world."

Anne Barrett Doyle, co-director of the watchdog group BishopAccountability.org, which tracks Catholic Church abuse allegations worldwide, called Vos Estis the most significant action Francis took on abuse. But she said the Vatican rarely makes clear whether an accused bishop's resignation represents punishment.
“The public is left in the dark,” she said.

Barrett Doyle said the Vatican has not released global disciplinary data comparable with figures it provided to a ‌United Nations committee ⁠in 2014. Her group relies on public records, media reports and investigations by prosecutors, governments and commissions to track cases.

She wants Leo to make permanent removal from ministry the universal rule for priests found under canon law to have sexually abused children, extending worldwide a policy adopted by US bishops in 2002.
"To say that no child molesters should be out to practice as priests is just such a no-brainer," she said. “It's a step that Leo could take now.”
Vatican officials have previously cited the difficulty of creating a single abuse reporting law across all countries and argued that removing priests can put them beyond Church supervision.

Angela Walker, executive director of the US-based Survivors Network of those Abused by Priests, said survivors increasingly turn to civil authorities because of the Church's "incredible failure" to police itself.
"There needs to be more transparency, more openness, and more accountability," she said. "I will believe it when I see it."
Survivors' long wait

In Mexico, ⁠survivors pressed the Vatican on clerical abuse decades before it became a defining crisis across Latin America. Among the most notorious cases was that of Marcial Maciel, the Mexican priest who founded the Legion of Christ order and whose accusers took allegations to the Vatican in the 1990s. The Vatican ordered Maciel in 2006 to withdraw from public ministry. He died in 2008, without ever facing his accusers.

The scale of his abuse became clearer after his death. In 2019, the Legion reported that Maciel had abused at least 60 minors, among 175 instances of child abuse the order documented involving 33 priests over eight ⁠decades.

José de Jesús Barba Martin, 87, alleged Maciel abused him when he was studying for the priesthood in the 1950s. He recalled survivors struggling to be heard by Church and state authorities in the late 1990s and said an appeal he sent Pope John Paul II went unanswered.
Decades later, that experience has left him with little expectation that another appeal to Rome would bring change.
“The Church is made up of two types of men: good and bad, courageous and cowardly," he said. "It will take a long time, and the issue will not be addressed ⁠under this pope nor the next."

Alberto Athié, 72, a former Mexican priest who pursued clerical abuse cases from inside the Church before leaving the priesthood in 2003, sees Leo's visit as another opportunity to push for transparency.
“I do have hope,” he said. “But my hope fades just the same ... Things have to be fixed within the Church."

Abuse survivor Sebastian Cuattromo said the Argentine Church should have been “at the international forefront” of confronting abuse under Argentine Pope Francis, but fell short of what he had hoped to see.
"There is a major outstanding debt," Cuattromo said.
Argentina's Episcopal Conference declined to comment.

headline: BTS gets unexpected football superstar visitor at Brazil concert
subheadline: Football legend Neymar spotted at BTS' Brazil concert with a special little guest
author: Web Desk
article_text:
BTS had an unexpected celebrity visitor during their Brazil concert and it was none other than football superstar Neymar.

The Brazilian footballer was spotted backstage at the group's highly anticipated ARIRANG World Tour stop, but the sweetest part of the outing involved a very special little guest accompanying him.

A video circulating on social media captured Neymar walking through a backstage hallway at the BTS concert alongside his young daughter, Maria Helena.

READ MORE: BTS shocks fans with new move after Brazil show ‘IDOL' walk gets cancelled

Dressed in a customized little BTS jacket, Helena appeared to be enjoying her special K-pop experience as the father-daughter duo greeted members of the staff with hugs.

However, it wasn’t Neymar but his daughter who is the real BTS fan in the family.

The two-year-old attended the group's opening-night concert in Brazil on Wednesday, October 28, at Estádio do Morumbis in São Paulo, accompanied by her mother, Amanda Kimberlly.

Neymar's backstage appearance was just a part of the special outing, rather than him attending the concert as a regular audience member.

According to her mother's social media updates, Helena is particularly fond of BTS member Jimin.

Amanda even shared glimpses of her daughter trying to get closer to the barrier, hoping the members would notice her.

headline: Romesh Ranganathan reveals he though he was 'going home' during 'Celebrity Traitors'
subheadline: The final drew in a huge 11.2 million viewers, making it the most-watched show of 2026 so far
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Romesh Ranganathan has spoken for the first time about his incredible victory on The Celebrity Traitors.

The comedian was crowned champion in Friday's final alongside actor Sebastian Croft, after they successfully banished Maya Jama and King Kenny from the castle.

Speaking on his BBC Radio 2 show hours after the final had aired, Romesh admitted his time on the show was 'full-on,' and admitted there were times when he thought he was about to be murdered.

READ MORE: BBC's ‘Celebrity Traitors' hit with setback as new tension arises

The final drew in a huge 11.2 million viewers, making it the most-watched show of 2026 so far.

Opening his show, Romesh was greeted with huge cheers from members of his crew as he announced himself as the 'winner of Celebrity Traitors.'

Sharing insight into his time in the famous castle, he said: 'I knew it was going to be immersive, but honestly I cannot explain to you how full-on it is.

'You are basically, the whole time, you're living that game, and imagine the situation where, obvs you're on camera, but you can't trust anyone you're talking to, fully.

'And that is your kind of existence it's such a weird thing, and equally I've known what's happened for a while, but there were so many moments in that game where I thought I was done for.

'When Rob, Leigh-Anne, Ross Kemp and myself were in the crypt, and they were deciding which one of us to murder, I just literally to me, I felt like I'd stuck my head above the parapet in the round table.

'I was joking around because obviously I wanted Leigh-Anne to have the key, but similarly I thought 'have I just exposed myself here?' Is this me done? And so that moment, when I hugged Claudia that was real, I genuinely thought I'm going home.

'Similarly I had no idea how much I'd been spoken about in terms of murder, that was weird to watch back.

'The shield challenge, where my pieces got moved, and I didn't complete the shield. I thought I'm definitely gonna get murdered tonight because obvs targeting me they've signalled that.

'And then, I know this sounds like faux humility, it's such a thin line between a great game and a terrible game as a faithful.

'When we, [Sebastian] and I won. I just cannot, it was just incredible, and there was a moment where I knew we'd won and Bash didn't.

Romesh later hosted another mini reunion on his BBC Radio 2 programme, along with his fellow champion Sebastian, 24, and their co-stars King Kenny and Leigh-Anne Pinnock joining him in the studio.

headline: NFL 'Sunday Ticket' antitrust case revived, court orders new trial on $4.7 billion damages
subheadline: The lawsuit was filed in 2015 by the Mucky Duck sports bar in San Francisco
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A federal appellate court on Friday, October 30, ruled that a judge’s decision to toss a $4.7 billion jury award in the suit was an error and forwarded the case back to district court for a new trial on damages.

The original verdict holding the NFL liable was reinstated.

The lawsuit stemmed from ‘NFL Sunday Ticket’ subscribers accusing the league, its teams and its network partners of working together to sell the out-of-market sports package at an inflated price and restrict competition.

The jury had awarded $4.7 billion in damages to subscribers in 2024, but U.S. District Judge Philip Gutierrez set aside the verdict after determining some expert testimony should have been excluded.

On Friday, October 30, a three-judge appellate panel ruled that Gutierrez’s decision was an abuse of the court’s discretion and that the testimony should have been allowed.

In its judgement, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals Judge Anthony D. Johnstone wrote, “Opinions are neither unfounded nor unreliable merely because they are impeachable.

“Such opinions are for the jury to weigh at trial. Once a jury does so, its verdict must stand unless it is clearly not supported by the evidence."

In a statement, NFL said, “We continue to believe that our media distribution strategy is by far the most fan-friendly distribution model in all of sports and entertainment.”

The lawsuit was filed in 2015 by the Mucky Duck sports bar in San Francisco.

On June 30, 2017, U.S. District Judge Beverly Reid O’Connell tossed the lawsuit, per Associated Press.

Two years later, the U.S. appellate court reinstated the case. In 2023 Gutierrez ruled the case could proceed as a class action, which happened in June 2024.

A federal appellate court on Friday, October 30, ruled that a judge’s decision to toss a $4.7 billion jury award in the suit was an error and forwarded the case back to district court for a new trial on damages.

The original verdict holding the NFL liable was reinstated.

The lawsuit stemmed from ‘NFL Sunday Ticket’ subscribers accusing the league, its teams and its network partners of working together to sell the out-of-market sports package at an inflated price and restrict competition.

The jury had awarded $4.7 billion in damages to subscribers in 2024, but U.S. District Judge Philip Gutierrez set aside the verdict after determining some expert testimony should have been excluded.

On Friday, October 30, a three-judge appellate panel ruled that Gutierrez’s decision was an abuse of the court’s discretion and that the testimony should have been allowed.

In its judgement, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals Judge Anthony D. Johnstone wrote, “Opinions are neither unfounded nor unreliable merely because they are impeachable.

The lawsuit was filed in 2015 by the Mucky Duck sports bar in San Francisco.

Two years later, the U.S. appellate court reinstated the case. In 2023 Gutierrez ruled the case could proceed as a class action, which happened in June 2024.

headline: Royal family makes big announcement with update on King Charles
subheadline: King Charles, Queen Camilla's photos and video released
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Buckingham Palace has released a delightful new update on King Charles and Queen Camilla as the royal couple touched down in Antigua and Barbuda to a warm and spectacular welcome.

The Palace announced that the King and Queen are joining celebrations marking the nation's 45th anniversary of Independence, ahead of attending the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2026.

Stunning new photos and videos from the historic visit have been shared on the royal family's official Instagram account, capturing the King's heartfelt connection with the people.

King, Queen surprised the world with their most crucial visit of the reign amid calls and growing crisis. Their visit is more than a royal occasion.

It represents an opportunity to reflect on a shared history, strengthen international friendships and look towards a future built on cooperation, respect and mutual understanding.

The celebrations also highlight the country's remarkable journey as an independent nation and its growing role within the Commonwealth.

Through engagements with communities, young people and environmental leaders, the visit places the spotlight on the values that truly shape a nation's future.

headline: What is TraderTraitor? Everything to know about hacking group behind binance heist
subheadline: Binance suffers record $6.3 billion crypto heist; North Korea suspected
author: Web Desk
article_text:
When $6.3 billion vanished from Binance’s wallets in about 20 minutes, blockchain analysts quickly pointed to one name: TraderTraitor.

Cybersecurity researchers and blockchain intelligence firms use TraderTraitor to refer to a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit.

It is widely considered part of the Lazarus Group, the broader umbrella name for Pyongyang’s cyber warfare apparatus, which has been linked to attacks since around 2009, including the 2014 Sony Pictures hack and the 2016 Bangladesh Bank heist.

The name “TraderTraitor” comes from a malware family that disguised itself as legitimate cryptocurrency trading software to lure industry professionals. According to TRM Labs, the unit is “North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” and the firm attributed the Binance attack to it “with high confidence,” citing “robust on- and off-chain intelligence.”

Chainalysis and Singapore-based Pangolin intelligence reached similar conclusions.

Its fingerprints were easy to detect. According to TRM, there were three similarities between the Binance hack and other cybercrimes carried out by North Korea, including the Bybit hack, involving a $1.5 billion theft in February 2025 and the KelpDAO hack, which took place in April 2026: small withdrawals from Tornado Cash; the preparation, which was done well ahead of the crime; and signatures collected in advance and executed all at once.

According to experts, this unit works as a means of generating income for the sanctions-hit regime. According to Dr Edward Howell from Oxford University, quoted by the BBC, "around 40 to 50% of North Korea's weapons of mass destruction programmes is funded by cyber and cryptocurrency warfare."

North Korea has been denying any involvement in those kinds of crimes. Its mission in Geneva has not commented on the allegations. However, the FBI has already linked TraderTraitor to major crypto thefts.
