headline: Iran's supreme leader orders 'geographically unrestricted' response to any US-Israeli threat
subheadline: Iran will determine “time and conditions” for ending war if US relaunches military campaign, says supreme leader
author: AFP
article_text:
Khamenei orders army to ensure “unrestricted response".
Supreme leader directs army to update target list.
Diplomatic efforts to avert war resumption underway.

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic Republic's foes of a possible resumption of strikes.

"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.

The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.

Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.

According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".

It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".

The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.

The supreme leader's statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were underway to avert a resumption of fighting.

A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance.

According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

headline: King Charles presented with unique gift after leaving conservationists impressed
subheadline: King Charles makes touching promise while planting tree in Bahamas
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles left conservationists impressed during his visit to Bonefish Pond National Park in the Bahamas.

King Charles was curious about the country's natural environment helped turn a royal engagement into a memorable occasion.

The monarch, who serves as patron of the Bahamas National Trust, visited the park in New Providence on Wednesday, meeting young people involved in the organisation's Education and Conservation Programme.

Read More: King Charles finds shady spot before hearing First Lady's plans

The Bahamas National Trust later shared its gratitude for the royal visit, recalling the King's memorable words to the nation, “I reach! Amen.”

During his visit, Charles heard how they teach young people about stewardship and the importance of preserving the Bahamas' natural beauty for future generations.

He also learned about the vital role coastal wetlands play in protecting the environment, particularly during high tides.

The head of the foundation revealed that the King asked so many questions during his tour that he ended up partially leading it himself.

After being introduced to the silver buttonwood tree, known for its ability to thrive in salty coastal conditions, Charles joined the organisation's Director of Science, Lindy Knowles, to plant a buttonwood tree.

As he planted it, the King offered a hopeful remark about its future growth, saying: “I hope to see you taller and stronger when I return.”

Charles also received a special red mangrove print created by coloured pencil artist Kim Smith as a memento of his visit.

Read More: Royal family makes big announcement with update on King Charles

headline: Elvis Presley Granddaughter reacts as Harry Styles channels the late legend
subheadline: Riley Keough has the sweetest reaction to Harry Styles' Elvis Presley transformation at MSG
author: Javeria Shahid
article_text:
Harry Styles' Elvis Presley-inspired Harryween performance got a special seal of approval from someone with a particularly close connection to the legendary King of Rock and Roll.

Presley's granddaughter, actress Riley Keough, was spotted enjoying the Watermelon Sugar hitmaker’s Halloween concert at Madison Square Garden.

A video circulating on social media shows the Daisy Jones & The Six star watching Harry perform at his October 30, Harryween show in New York City.

READ MORE: Harry Styles dresses as Elvis Presley for 'Harryween' night

Standing in the stands alongside Zoë, Anne and Gemma, the actress appeared completely caught up in the performance.

She was seen singing along, dancing, recording the moment on her phone and smiling throughout the show.

The clip captures the Under The Bridge actress enjoying the Golden singer’s performance of his hit song Watermelon Sugar, as he took the stage dressed in an Presley-inspired look.

Harry opened the Halloween concert channeling the late music icon, making the evening particularly special for fans of both artists.

The actress's presence made the performance even more noteworthy, given her family connection to Elvis.

Moreover, later that night, the As It Was singer also recreated his The X Factor audition look from 2010.

READ MORE: Harry Styles recreates his 16-year-old ‘X Factor' audition look at Harryween

headline: ‘Jessica Jones' star Krysten Ritter shares haunting Halloween look in selfie
subheadline: Krysten Ritter will share the screen with Charlie Cox once again
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Krysten Ritter has found a fun way to celebrate Halloween, and her latest pictures are already catching fans' attention.

The actress, best known for playing Jessica Jones in the Marvel series, shared two photos on social media to show how she was spending the spooky holiday.

Ritter kept her look simple but stayed true to her love for dark fashion. She wore a black shirt with a scary pumpkin face on it, along with ripped black jeans and black boots.

READ MORE: Krysten Ritter unveils rare impact of playing strong women on personal life

Her black bangs and bright red lipstick completed the look. She also shared a mirror selfie that showed her full outfit.

Fans also had something else to look at in the background. A poster of Elvira: Mistress of the Dark could be seen on her wall, while a Jessica Jones poster was placed nearby.

The little details made the pictures even more special for Marvel fans.

But Halloween is not the only reason Ritter has been making headlines. The actress is also getting ready to play Jessica Jones again in the second season of Daredevil: Born Again on Disney+.

She will share the screen with Charlie Cox once again. Ritter has also expressed her happiness about returning, saying there is still more to tell about Jessica's story.

The Scott Street hitmaker has a strict no-phone policy at her tour so fans were unable to capture the monumental moment, but they later took to social media and gushed over the unbelievable experience.

headline: Once Upon a Farm Tractor wheels recall: Everything parents need to know
subheadline: FDA warns of potentially fatal choking hazard in Once Upon a Farm Tractor toddler bars
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has warned consumers not to buy or serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler soft-baked bars, citing a potentially fatal choking hazard.

The advisory, issued October 30, 2026, covers all flavours, quantities, varieties, lot codes, and expiration dates.

According to the FDA, several reports describe toddlers aged 1.5 to 2.5 years suffering “complete airway obstruction with the inability to breathe” after eating the product.

When chewed, the bars reportedly form a “dry, sticky mass” that standard choking interventions, including back blows and the Heimlich manoeuvre, may fail to dislodge. Some incidents required emergency response intervention and hospital observation.

The product is sold nationwide online and at major retailers including Costco, Target and Walmart, and may also be available through Amazon and other third-party vendors. The recalled varieties include Apple, Sweet Potato and Spinach; Strawberry, Pumpkin and Beet; and Banana, Pumpkin and Cauliflower.

The FDA said it informed the company of the adverse event reports, and Once Upon a Farm has agreed to initiate a voluntary recall. Consumers are advised to throw the product away immediately and not to open or use it. Retailers have been told to stop selling the bars.

In a statement, the company said: “We know that parents place their trust in us every time they buy one of our products. We fell short of that, and that is why we are taking these aggressive actions.”

Once Upon a Farm is offering full refunds for products returned to the place of purchase, or consumers can contact [email protected].

The FDA urged anyone experiencing choking to call emergencies if first aid measures fail, and encouraged consumers to report complaints through its Industry and Consumer Assistance portal.

headline: CM Maryam calls Capt Safdar's remarks about women, cancer patients ‘heartbreaking' amid backlash
subheadline: "Some battles are fought in silence, and some wounds are invisible," Maryam writes on X
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Captain (retd) Muhammad Safdar's remarks about women and cancer patients have triggered a backlash on social media, with his wife, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, expressing regret over his comments.

Speaking at a Khatm-e-Nabuwwat gathering in Chiniot earlier this week, Safdar criticised the slogan Mera Jism, Meri Marzi (My Body, My Choice), questioning why women who assert control over their bodies seek prayers and religious intervention when diagnosed with serious illnesses such as cancer.

He argued that women who claim ownership over their bodies should also be able to cure themselves if they fall ill, adding that the human body ultimately remains under God's control.

“Those who advocate ‘My Body, My Choice’ turn to religious scholars for prayers and blessed water when they are diagnosed with serious illnesses such as cancer. If they insist that their bodies are entirely their own, they should also have the ability to cure themselves. Ultimately, the human body is governed by God.”

On Friday, CM Maryam responded to a post on X about Safdar's remarks, describing the situation as “heartbreaking” and referring to the struggles women face behind closed doors.

“Heartbreaking. The silent battles a woman, a wife, fights behind closed doors… The strength she must find even when she feels like breaking. Some battles are fought in silence, and some wounds are invisible,” she wrote on her official handle.

Amid the slamming of Safdar, people on social media also praised Maryam for taking a stance publicly.

Former federal minister Fawad Chaudhry also praised the Punjab chief executive for taking a "clear stance".

“It takes real courage to take a public stand like this. More power to you, Maryam Nawaz Sharif,” journalist Benazir Shah wrote.

"My Maa jee has been a cancer patient, and God knows how we managed to get through those difficult times. Her survival was nothing short of a miracle," journalist Ajmal Jami said.

"Listening to Cap Safdar’s remarks on this matter is utterly shameful and disgraceful," he added.

headline: King Charles joins Antigua PM for anthem ceremony, Queen prepares to arrive
subheadline: King Charles's Guyana visit comes to an end with royal farewell at Cheddi Jagan Airport
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles's arrival followed the conclusion of his state visit to Guyana, where he was seen off at airport on Friday by senior officials, including Prime Minister Brigadier Mark Anthony Phillips and Foreign Affairs Minister Hugh Hilton Todd.

The monarch touched down at V.C. Bird International Airport at 7.48pm on Friday, October 30, marking his first visit to the country since becoming King.

Read More: King Charles presented with unique gift after leaving conservationists impressed

He was greeted on arrival by Prime Minister Gaston Browne, alongside Governor-General Rodney Williams and Lady Williams.

Minister of Works and Housing Maria Bird-Browne was also among the dignitaries waiting to welcome His Majesty.

Foreign Affairs Minister E.P. Chet Greene and national hero Sir Vivian Richards were also present for the royal arrival.

As Charles stood on the airport dais, the Antigua and Barbuda Defence Force Band performed the national anthems of both countries, beginning with Britain's 'God Save the King' before playing 'Fair Antigua and Barbuda'.

Queen Camilla will accompany her husband during the engagements linked to the gathering.

headline: Prince William's deafening silence leaves Harry in tears
subheadline: Prince William is acting like Prince Harry and Meghan Markle don't exist anymore
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William has moved Prince Harry to tears with his unbreakable silence and continued reluctance to make amends.

The Prince of Wales has made it clear to Harry that he won't forgive him, even after the Duke's UK move.

The future monarch has not even responded to the Duke of Sussex's efforts to arrange a meeting, a source claimed.

READ MORE: Prince Harry's biggest fear about William laid bare

"William, 44, has remained silent on reunion and reconciliation request, acting like Harry and Meghan don't exist," according to an insider.

"The heir to the British throne's deafening silence is eating the Duke inside," they added.

William's refusal to make amends infuriates Harry. The insider added that the Duke has reached out to his elder brother in the hopes of setting up a sit-down to clear the air.

However, William turned a deaf ear to the request and kept mum. He did not even respond to Archie and Lilibet's father's emotional plea, which has made the Duke run out of patience.

"Harry's known to be impulsive, and the more wound up he gets, the more likely he is to follow through on threats to make William regret this," they added.

William has seemingly not recovered from Harry's past attacks. Meanwhile, King Charles, 77, wants his children to mend fences, if for no other reason than to protect the reputation of the monarchy.

However, William is still refusing to come to the table, seemingly defying the monarch by openly going against his wish.

After Prince William's persistent resistance, King Charles was forced to release a terse letter declaring that his son and daughter-in-law would remain "non-working royals," a powerful missive widely seen as a preemptive strike to keep the couple firmly outside the royal embrace.

headline: Macklemore makes major statement after Ed Sheeran stage moment+
subheadline: Macklemore's European tour began in Dublin
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Macklemore has made it clear that he no longer wants to stay quiet about Palestine, using his latest London concert to speak about the suffering of children in Gaza.

The rapper addressed thousands of fans during his sold out show at OVO Arena Wembley on Friday. He explained that seeing the situation unfold online made him feel he could no longer remain silent.

"At a certain point, it was more uncomfortable for me to stay silent than to say something," he told the crowd.

READ MORE: Ed Sheeran suffers huge Instagram follower drop amid tour row

He also said speaking up was not about being brave but about showing basic humanity. His comments received loud cheers from fans, who joined in chants of "Free Palestine".

Singer Paloma Faith also appeared on stage and spoke about why every child's life matters. She questioned why her own children should be considered more important than children in Gaza, Sudan, Yemen and Congo.

Climate campaigner Greta Thunberg also addressed the audience, saying donations and benefit concerts alone would not bring change. She called for action through actual policy changes.

READ MORE: ‘Jessica Jones' star Krysten Ritter shares haunting Halloween look in selfie

Macklemore's European tour began in Dublin before moving to Paris and London. All proceeds from the concerts will support organisations providing medical care, education and humanitarian help to Palestinians.

headline: What time is trick or treating? 2026 hours explained
subheadline: Halloween falls on Saturday, October 31, 2026
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Halloween falls on Saturday in 2026 for the first time since 2020, giving families more time for costumes and candy.

There are no universal trick-or-treat hours, and schedules vary widely by community. However, usually trick-or-treating hours run between 4:00 p.m. and 9:30 p.m.

Communities are usually advised to follow local guidelines if there are any set trick-or-treating times. General standard hours for toddlers are 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m., standard kickoff is 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., peak hours are 5:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. and winding down is around 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.

In New Jersey, there are no set hours for the state; rather, the town sets its schedule. In towns that have posted 2026 schedules, the most frequent time slot is between 3 and 8 p.m., according to the statewide database.

Some places are changing their times around: Collingswood’s times are noon to 7 p.m.; Haddon Heights, 3 to 8 p.m.; and Medford, noon to 8 p.m. There are five towns in Ocean County: Toms River, Beachwood, Pine Beach, South Toms River and Island Heights, trick-or-treating one day earlier, from 4 to 8 p.m. Friday, Oct. 30, in order not to conflict with the yearly Toms River Halloween Parade.

Atlanta usually follows 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., Boston schedueles it for 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m., Chicago observes 3:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

While in Houston it is for 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., in Los Angeles it is 6:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., New York City there's 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. and Seattle observes 4:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

Post advised some house-to-house advice: a light on the porch indicates participation, a dark one means moving on, and a kid gives a good knock but does not ring over and over again. She encouraged homeowners to allow children to pick their candies at their leisure.

headline: Taylor Swift's 'Cleveland' marks big milestone despite brutal criticism

headline: Prince William, Princess Kate's secret mission exposed
subheadline: The Prince and Princess of Wales quietly upping their game amid royal uproars
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William and Princess Kate are quietly upping their game, focused not on titles and tradition, but on a bigger mission to bring sparkle back to the monarchy and deliver real change without needing to be the centre of attention.

William proved it in the most unexpected way. At 44, he was at his witty, disarming best on The Graham Norton Show alongside Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham and Robert Irwin Jr. He wasn't there for royal protocol.

He was there to champion his Earthshot Prize, joking about a 12-foot crocodile named after him and his secret life on Aston Villa forums. When he confessed his fantasy of being a DJ despite a pre-determined destiny, the clip exploded with 1.2 million likes.

READ MORE: Prince William's deafening silence leaves Harry in tears

Fans called it a defining moment. "He's making the Royal Family a lot more relatable and not so stuffy," one wrote.

While others praised a breath of fresh air with no etiquette hurdles. That appearance was not a one-off, it is the new blueprint.

Determined to shed the Palace's figurehead image, William is rolling up his sleeves and getting stuck into what he believes in.

Earlier this month he closed The Mall and turned it into a backyard cricket pitch, playing alongside legends like Joe Root, Sourav Ganguly and Brian Lara to highlight the unifying power of sport.

There were no curtsies, no briefings, just purpose.

From a casual pint with Eugene Levy at Windsor Castle to a surprise appearance on Travis and Jason Kelce’s podcast just hours before Travis married Taylor Swift, Prince William is showing up where no royal has before.

And when he and Kate lit up Tom Cruise’s premiere, even Cruise was star-struck, saying: “They’re just beautiful people and fun!”

It’s clear that the Waleses are rewriting the rules with less secrecy and more heart.

headline: Harmer, Rabada steer South Africa to series win over Australia
subheadline: Chasing 288-run target, Australia bowled out for 111, handing hosts 2-1 win in three-match series
author: Reuters
article_text:
Harmer claims career-best figures of 6-16.
Kagiso Rabada reaches 350 Test wickets.
South Africa reclaim top Test ranking spot.

South Africa spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 and Kagiso Rabada became the fastest by balls bowled to reach 350 test wickets as the hosts thumped Australia by 176 runs to clinch their three-match series 2-1 at Newlands on Saturday.

Set a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the test world rankings for the first time since January 2016.

Australia had hopes of chasing down the total but lost two wickets in the first over of the final day and slumped to 62 for eight as their effort became a battle of survival that South Africa ended before tea.

There will be questions asked of this Australia side in the wake of the defeat, not least another poor batting display and the decision to bowl on the opening morning that left them batting last on a wearing wicket.

"The trend of this game was once you got yourself in there were runs to be had," Australia captain Pat Cummins said. "But within the first hour the game was away from us and we did not give ourselves a chance.

"We are a really good side but playing tough opponents away from home is always difficult. We came here thinking we were good enough to win but we couldn't do it."

Hopes of victory evaporated in the first half hour as Rabada (3-39) removed the top three batters to take his tally to 350 test wickets, taking 13,808 deliveries, fewer than compatriot Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan’s Waqar Younis (14,905).

After that Harmer came into his own, exploiting the conditions expertly to also claim a first 10-wicket haul in tests with figures of 10-120 across the match.

Rabada removed opener Matt Renshaw (0), caught by wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton down the leg side, and the struggling Marnus Labuschagne (4) leg before wicket in the first over of the innings

He then had the dangerous Travis Head caught at gully by Marco Jansen to rock Australia early on.

First-innings centurion Josh Inglis (4) was run out attempting a quick single to compound Australia’s woes, and from there Harmer took the last six wickets.

Cummins (11 from 90 balls) and innings top-scorer Nathan Lyon (33 not out) delayed the inevitable with a ninth-wicket stand that lasted 17.2 overs, but Harmer trapped the former lbw and then bowled Josh Hazlewood to seal the win.

"It was just understanding what I needed to do, getting the ball in the right areas as often as I could, and playing with my pace and trajectories, the little nuances I have learnt along the way. It all worked out alright," Harmer said.

"Today was a lot of fun, fielders around the bat and trying to get the win. That is the stuff of dreams for a spinner."

The victory also keeps alive South Africa's hopes of defending their World Test Championship title next year, having beaten Australia at Lord's in the previous decider in 2025.

headline: ‘First arrest, then decide charges': Khawaja Asif assails govts over political victimisation
subheadline: Defence czar recalls being detained four times, says political victimisation is never in the country's interest
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Asif recalls imprisonment at Attock Fort during Musharraf's era.
Says mediator Pakistan plays a historic role in US-Iran conflict.
Adds educated youth can contribute to national development.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has criticised the practice of political victimisation, saying governments often arrest people first and decide later what charges to bring against them.

"Civilian governments, when they want to arrest someone, first arrest them and then think about what charge to bring," he said while speaking to reporters in Sialkot on Saturday.

His remarks come amid continued tensions between the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the main opposition party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), which has repeatedly accused the federal government of political victimisation, citing the imprisonment of its founder, Imran Khan, and several other party leaders.

The opposition has also criticised the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, which rendered the PTI-led provincial government non-functional.

Dysfunctional chief minister Sohail Afridi and several members of his cabinet were taken into 'preventive custody' following the federal government's move.

The Imran Khan-founded party condemned the detentions as politically motivated, while the federal government maintained that the measures were necessary to address the province's worsening security situation and counter terrorism.

Asif recalls imprisonment

Recalling his own political struggles, the defence czar said he had been imprisoned four times, including at Attock Fort during former military ruler Pervez Musharraf's era.

Asif said he spent six months in the National Accountability Bureau's (NAB) custody during the PTI government's tenure in 2020, adding that those who detained him could not even explain the charges against him.

The federal minister further said he had repeatedly asked anti-graft watchdog officials what allegations had been levelled against him, adding that political victimisation is never in the country's interest.

He said he entered politics in 1991 and had been serving the country for 36 years, during which he witnessed numerous ups and downs.

The minister also said he sometimes felt tired but remained committed to serving Sialkot, calling the city his identity and the welfare of its people his responsibility.

Exchange with Fazl

Khawaja Asif also alluded to his recent exchange with Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, saying he had urged him in the National Assembly to revisit his political narrative.

The minister added that he had met the JUI-F chief in the National Assembly two days back and felt that Fazlur Rehman still had the energy to remain politically active.

Pakistan's diplomatic role

Turning to foreign affairs, the defence minister said Pakistan is playing a historic role in efforts to resolve the Iran-US conflict and address differences between Iran and its Arab neighbours.

He said Pakistan's diplomatic efforts under Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir's leadership are continuing, adding that the country has attained an international standing of which its people could be proud.

Asif said he had represented Pakistan at the defence agreements signed in Makkah and Doha.

Pakistan, he went on to say, has shown the Islamic world that overseas military bases could not necessarily guarantee the security of host countries, arguing that such facilities served the interests of the powers operating them and were intended to protect Israel.

The minister also said Pakistan had defeated an enemy five times its size during the latest conflict with India.

He said previous wars had left some ambiguity over their outcomes, but there was no such uncertainty this time, as India and its military had acknowledged the outcome.

Asif also highlighted the armed forces' prolonged fight against terrorism, saying they had continued to make sacrifices in defence of the country.

Youth and education

The defence minister described young people as Pakistan's valuable asset, saying educated and skilled youth could play an important role in national development.

He said the education sector had evolved over time but remarked that politicians were generally reluctant to take charge of the education ministry because they saw little political benefit in it.

The federal minister further said he had repeatedly asked anti-graft watchdog officials what allegations had been levelled against him, adding that political victimisation is never in the country's interest.

He said he entered politics in 1991 and had been serving the country for 36 years, during which he witnessed numerous ups and downs.

Turning to foreign affairs, the defence minister said Pakistan is playing a historic role in efforts to resolve the Iran-US conflict and address differences between Iran and its Arab neighbours.

He said Pakistan's diplomatic efforts under Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir's leadership are continuing, adding that the country has attained an international standing of which its people could be proud.

The defence minister described young people as Pakistan's valuable asset, saying educated and skilled youth could play an important role in national development.

headline: Kate Middleton receives sad news from sister Pippa after major setback at £15m home
subheadline: Kate Middleton's sister Pippa told to tear up unauthorised car park at lavish estate
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Kate Middleton has received disappointing news involving her younger sister Pippa Matthews.

Pippa and her husband, hedge fund manager James Matthews have been told by West Berkshire Council to tear up the car park at their £15.5million Barton Court estate in the village of Kintbury.

The couple bought the 145-acre property, formerly owned by designer Sir Terence Conran, in 2022.

However, their plans for part of the estate have now run into trouble after they laid around 400 square metres of hard standing on a former paddock without first securing planning permission.

The development has also caused upset among local residents, who were reportedly shocked to find that a stretch of meadowland on the approach to their village had been turned into a private parking area for anglers visiting the estate's fishing facilities.

Villagers raised their concerns with the council, arguing that the work had been carried out without any consultation.

Planning inspectors later found that the car park was damaging the surrounding countryside. They also concluded that the development had taken away from the rural character of the North Wessex Downs.

James and Pippa's representatives attempted to secure permission retrospectively through an application submitted in November last year.

West Berkshire Council rejected the application in February. The estate then appealed, but a Government-appointed inspector dismissed the challenge in July, agreeing that the car park was out of keeping with its countryside surroundings.

Locals had claimed the path had been used by villagers for generations, with one resident telling The Times: "I taught my son to ride his bike on that path."

The dispute left some residents unhappy, with one describing the atmosphere as carrying "a lot of ill will and residual anger".

The development has also caused upset among local residents, who were reportedly shocked to find that a stretch of meadowland on the approach to their village had been turned into a private parking area for anglers visiting the estate's fishing facilities.

Villagers raised their concerns with the council, arguing that the work had been carried out without any consultation.

Planning inspectors later found that the car park was damaging the surrounding countryside. They also concluded that the development had taken away from the rural character of the North Wessex Downs.

James and Pippa's representatives attempted to secure permission retrospectively through an application submitted in November last year.

Locals had claimed the path had been used by villagers for generations, with one resident telling The Times: "I taught my son to ride his bike on that path."

The dispute left some residents unhappy, with one describing the atmosphere as carrying "a lot of ill will and residual anger".

For some villagers, the latest car park ruling has brought back familiar frustrations, with one resident dismissing the development as "not very village-y".

headline: Turkiye nominates Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu for UN's top job
subheadline: Turkish President Erdogan says nomination reflects Ankara's commitment to "effective multilateralism"
author: AFP
article_text:
ISTANBUL: Turkiye has nominated Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, head of the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), to be the next UN secretary-general, a diplomatic source confirmed on Saturday.

The move came after a deadlock in the selection process, with the latest straw poll at the UN Security Council held on Friday returning an inconclusive outcome.

Contacted by AFP, the Turkish diplomatic source confirmed that the nomination letter dated Friday from Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan was submitted to the presidents of the UN General Assembly and the Security Council.

In the letter, published by Turkish media, Erdogan said the nomination reflected Ankara's commitment to "effective multilateralism" at a time when "geopolitical divisions are deepening and trust between nations is diminishing".

With more than four decades of experience in international relations and diplomacy, Sinirlioglu has held some of Turkiye's highest diplomatic positions, including foreign minister and permanent representative to the United Nations, Erdogan said in the letter.

The choice of next UN chief would be crucial in steering the international community towards "a more peaceful, just and sustainable future" amid mounting global challenges, he added.

The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31.

Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 available in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided.

Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.
